title: PixFmt / BitDepth / EncoderId and exhaustive pix_fmt_for
description: Create the pixel-format layer of transcodarr-core::plan. Define EncoderId, BitDepth and PixFmt as #[non_exhaustive] enums (reuse BitDepth/EncoderId from the S3 facts / S4 policy modules if those tasks already defined them — in that case re-export, do NOT duplicate) and implement pix_fmt_for as a single exhaustive `match` over (EncoderId, BitDepth). Contract deviation to note in the doc comment: the architecture lists `pix_fmt_for(enc, depth) -> PixFmt`, but EncoderId also covers audio encoders and NVENC has no 12-bit path, so the return type is `Result<PixFmt, CoreError>`; the match itself remains exhaustive with no wildcard arm, so adding an encoder is a compile error. Add `CoreError::UnsupportedPixFmt { encoder, bit_depth }` to the existing thiserror CoreError enum. This encodes the measured rule: libx265 10-bit => yuv420p10le, hevc_nvenc 10-bit => p010le, 8-bit sources map to yuv420p and are NEVER upconverted.

impl PixFmt { pub const fn as_ffmpeg(self) -> &'static str }
impl BitDepth { pub fn from_bits(bits: u32) -> Option<BitDepth> }
impl EncoderId { pub const fn as_ffmpeg(self) -> &'static str; pub const fn is_video(self) -> bool }

title: StreamMap, StreamAction and output-index resolution
description: Create the per-stream mapping model that makes R40 (preserve ALL audio and subtitle tracks) structural. A StreamMap is an ordered list of entries, one per source stream, each carrying an explicit action: Copy, Encode(EncodeSpec) or Drop. The critical piece is `output_index_of`, which returns the per-kind ordinal a kept stream will occupy in the output — that ordinal is what later drives ffmpeg stream specifiers like `-c:a:1` and `-b:a:1`, and getting it wrong silently applies an audio bitrate to the wrong track. Validation in `StreamMap::new` rejects duplicate source indices, non-ascending source indices, and a map where every entry is Drop. No ffmpeg strings are emitted here; this task is pure data plus index arithmetic.
apis: #[non_exhaustive] pub enum StreamKind { Video, Audio, Subtitle, Attachment, Data }
pub struct Disposition { pub default: bool, pub forced: bool }
pub struct EncodeSpec { pub encoder: EncoderId, pub bitrate: Option<String>, pub channels: Option<u16>, pub pix_fmt: Option<PixFmt>, pub extra_args: Vec<String> }
#[non_exhaustive] pub enum StreamAction { Copy, Encode(EncodeSpec), Drop }
pub struct StreamMapEntry { pub source_index: u32, pub kind: StreamKind, pub action: StreamAction, pub language: Option<String>, pub title: Option<String>, pub disposition: Disposition }
pub struct StreamMap { /* private Vec<StreamMapEntry> */ }

impl StreamMap { pub fn new(entries: Vec<StreamMapEntry>) -> Result<Self, CoreError>; pub fn entries(&self) -> &[StreamMapEntry]; pub fn kept(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &StreamMapEntry>; pub fn count_of(&self, kind: StreamKind) -> u32; pub fn output_index_of(&self, source_index: u32) -> Option<(StreamKind, u32)>; pub fn has_encode(&self) -> bool }
impl StreamKind { pub const fn ffmpeg_specifier(self) -> &'static str /* v|a|s|t|d */ }

title: DecoderTriple, DecodeOption and decode_matrix_for
description: Create the decode-strategy matrix: an ORDERED list of decode options the agent may try, first viable wins, with the software option always present and always last. Each option pairs a DecoderTriple (codec, profile, bit_depth, kind) with the argv prefix that selects it. This is the type that makes hardware decode per-codec rather than a global flag (the Turing lesson: NVDEC cannot decode AV1 at all and cannot decode 10-bit H.264). This task only BUILDS the matrix from an allow-list of DecoderKinds; deciding which kinds an agent actually supports is capability-matching territory and is out of scope. NVDEC prefix is `["-hwaccel", "cuda"]` (decode into system memory) — the `-hwaccel_output_format cuda` full-GPU pipeline is explicitly out of scope and must be noted as such in the module doc. If DecoderTriple/DecoderKind were already introduced by S4's capability module, re-export rather than redefine.
apis: #[non_exhaustive] pub enum DecoderKind { Software, Nvdec, Qsv, Vaapi, VideoToolbox }
pub struct DecoderTriple { pub codec: String, pub profile: String, pub bit_depth: u32, pub kind: DecoderKind }
pub struct DecodeOption { pub triple: DecoderTriple, pub argv_prefix: Vec<String> }
pub struct DecodeStrategyMatrix { pub options: Vec<DecodeOption> }
pub fn decode_matrix_for(codec: &str, profile: Option<&str>, bit_depth: u32, allowed: &[DecoderKind]) -> DecodeStrategyMatrix
impl DecodeStrategyMatrix { pub fn software_only(codec: &str, profile: Option<&str>, bit_depth: u32) -> Self; pub fn software(&self) -> &DecodeOption }
impl DecoderKind { pub const fn as_label(self) -> &'static str; pub fn argv_prefix(self) -> Vec<String> }

title: Per-stream map and codec argument emitter
description: Implement the inner half of argv construction: given a StreamMap, emit the explicit `-map` selectors and the per-stream codec arguments. This is deliberately a standalone pure function so it can be tested exhaustively without a full plan. Rules: emit one `-map 0:<source_index>` per KEPT entry in source order (never `-map 0`, so a Drop is honoured and so the intent is auditable); then, for each kept entry, emit `-c:<spec>:<output_index> copy` for Copy or `-c:<spec>:<output_index> <encoder>` for Encode, where `<spec>` comes from `StreamKind::ffmpeg_specifier`. For an Encode entry additionally emit, in this fixed order: `-b:a:<i> <bitrate>` and `-ac:<i> <channels>` for audio, `-pix_fmt:v:<i> <pix_fmt>` for video, then the entry's `extra_args` verbatim. Every emitted token is a separate Vec element — no spaces inside a token, no shell quoting, ever.
apis: pub(crate) fn emit_stream_args(map: &StreamMap) -> Result<Vec<String>, CoreError>

title: build_ffmpeg_argv assembly with chapters, metadata and attachments
description: Implement the public argv builder that assembles a complete ffmpeg argument vector, EXCLUDING argv[0] (the agent supplies its own ffmpeg path; the server never names an executable). Order is fixed and must be asserted by test: global flags (`-hide_banner`, `-nostdin`, `-y` when overwrite), `-progress <progress_file>` and `-nostats`, the chosen decode option's argv_prefix, `-i <source>`, the output of emit_stream_args, then `-map_metadata 0` (when MetadataPolicy::CopyGlobal) / `-map_metadata -1` (Strip), `-map_chapters 0` when copy_chapters (else `-map_chapters -1`), attachment mapping `-map 0:t?` plus `-c:t copy` when copy_attachments and the container supports it (mkv only — mp4 has no attachment streams, so the flags are suppressed), one `-disposition:<spec>:<i> <default|forced|default+forced|0>` per kept stream whose disposition is non-empty, `-threads <n>` when set, `plan.extra_output_args`, `-f <ffmpeg_format>`, and finally the temp output path. Provide the contract-named `build_ffmpeg_argv(plan, paths)` which uses the software decode option, plus `build_ffmpeg_argv_with_decode(plan, paths, Option<&DecodeOption>)` for the agent's chosen accel.

title: Plan builders: EncodePlan from an audio or video Decision
description: Bridge the policy layer (S4's AudioPlan / VideoPlan and the S3 FileFacts + per-stream rows) to an EncodePlan. Two constructors. `plan_for_audio` maps EVERY source stream (video Copy, subtitles Copy, attachments Copy, data Copy) and sets Encode only on the audio stream indices listed in AudioPlan::streams, choosing bitrate from `bitrate_by_channels` by exact channel count with fallback to the highest entry <= the track's channels; all other audio tracks are Copy, never Drop. `plan_for_video` sets Encode on the single video stream with `pix_fmt_for(encoder, facts.video_bit_depth)` and copies everything else, and builds the decode matrix from the source video codec/profile/bit depth. Neither constructor performs I/O. The `-map`-everything default is the structural fix for the observed `-c:a eac3 drops every track but the default` bug.

title: Create paths module skeleton and PathError

Create `crates/transcodarr-core/src/paths/error.rs` defining:

#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum PathError {
    #[error("path is empty")]
    Empty,
    #[error("path must be absolute: {path}")]
    NotAbsolute { path: String },
    #[error("path escapes the filesystem root: {path}")]
    TraversalAboveRoot { path: String },
    #[error("mount prefix must be an absolute canonical path: {prefix}")]
    InvalidMount { prefix: String },
    #[error("no mount covers canonical path: {path}")]

title: Capability module scaffold + decoder capability types
description:
Create the `capability` module inside `transcodarr-core` and implement the decoder half of the capability model. This is the type-level encoding of the measured Turing facts: NVDEC cannot decode AV1 (hard fail) and cannot decode 10-bit H.264 (soft CPU fallback that still exits 0). Define, with `///` docs on every public item (clippy `missing-docs-in-crate-items` is on):

- `#[non_exhaustive] pub enum DecoderKind { Software, Nvdec, Qsv, Vaapi, VideoToolbox }` — serde `snake_case`, `Copy`, `Eq`, `Hash`, `Ord`.
- `#[non_exhaustive] pub enum DecoderStatus { Untested, VerifiedOk, VerifiedSoftFallback, VerifiedFail }` — serde `snake_case`, `Copy`, `Eq`, `Ord`, plus `pub const fn satisfies_hardware(self) -> bool` returning `true` ONLY for `VerifiedOk`, and `pub const fn as_label(self) -> &'static str` (exhaustive match, snake_case, used as a metric label).
- `pub struct DecoderTriple { pub codec: String, pub profile: String, pub bit_depth: u32, pub kind: DecoderKind }` with `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize`, plus:
  - `pub fn new(codec: impl Into<String>, profile: impl Into<String>, bit_depth: u32, kind: DecoderKind) -> Self` which lowercases and trims `codec` and `profile` on construction (normalisation happens once, here).
  - `pub fn matches(&self, required: &DecoderTriple) -> bool` — `self` is an advertised capability entry, `required` is what a job asks for. Equal on `codec`, `bit_depth`, `kind`; `profile` matches if either side is empty (wildcard) or the two are equal.
  - `impl std::fmt::Display` producing the stable form `"{kind}:{codec}:{profile}:{bit_depth}"` with empty profile rendered as `*` (e.g. `nvdec:av1:*:8`).
- `pub struct DecoderCapability { pub triple: DecoderTriple, pub status: DecoderStatus, pub evidence: String, pub probed_at_unix: i64 }` with the same derives minus `Hash`/`Ord`.

Also add `pub mod capability;` to `crates/transcodarr-core/src/lib.rs` and `mod decoder; pub use decoder::*;` in the new `capability/mod.rs`. No I/O, no async, no external crate beyond `serde`.

title: Requirement, Requirements and UnmetRequirement types
description:
Define the requirement vocabulary a job declares and the typed reason a match fails. `Requirement` is `#[non_exhaustive]` specifically so that adding a variant without handling it in `satisfies()` (S3-005) is a compile error.

title: satisfies(): the single capability gate
description:
Implement the one function that decides whether an agent may be offered a job. Server and agent both link this exact code, so agent-side re-validation is a genuine detector of a stale server capability model rather than a second implementation.

Create `crates/transcodarr-core/src/capability/satisfies.rs` with:

```rust
pub fn satisfies(cap: &Capability, req: &Requirements) -> Result<(), UnmetRequirement>;
pub fn satisfies_one(cap: &Capability, req: &Requirement) -> Result<(), UnmetRequirement>;
```

`satisfies` evaluates items in declaration order and returns the FIRST failure. `satisfies_one` is a single `match` over `Requirement` that must be exhaustive (no `_ =>` arm — that is the compile-time guard that a future variant cannot be silently unchecked). Per-variant rules:
- `AgentClass(c)` → `cap.has_class(c)` else `UnmetReason::Missing`.
- `Encoder(e)` / `Muxer(m)` → `cap.has_encoder`/`has_muxer` else `Missing`.
- `Decoder(t)` → let `s = cap.decoder_status(t)`. If `t.kind == DecoderKind::Software`, satisfied unless `s == VerifiedFail`. Otherwise satisfied ONLY when `s.satisfies_hardware()` (i.e. `VerifiedOk`); `Untested`, `VerifiedSoftFallback` and `VerifiedFail` all fail with `UnmetReason::DecoderUnusable(s)`. The `VerifiedSoftFallback` rejection is the Turing Hi10-H.264 lesson expressed as a type rule: the job that "works" on CPU while occupying an NVENC slot must never be offered.
- `MinEffectiveCores(w)` → `cap.effective_cores >= w` else `InsufficientCores { have, want }`.
- `MinFreeBytes { path, bytes }` → resolve `cap.mount_covering(path)`; `None` → `NoMountCovers`; else `mount.free_bytes >= bytes` or `InsufficientFreeBytes`.
- `MountCovers(p)` → `cap.mount_covering(p).is_some()` else `NoMountCovers`.
- `LabelEquals { key, value }` → `cap.label(key) == Some(value)` else `LabelMismatch { have }`.
- `PlatformIn(list)` → `list.contains(&cap.platform)` else `PlatformMismatch { have }`.

Re-export `satisfies` from `crates/transcodarr-core/src/lib.rs` as a crate-root item (`pub use capability::satisfies;`) since the architecture references it as `transcodarr_core::satisfies`.

pub fn satisfies_one(cap: &Capability, req: &Requirement) -> Result<(), UnmetRequirement>

title: Capability overrides: learned negatives with expiry
description:
Implement the override layer that lets an observed runtime failure feed back into the capability model without becoming a permanent, unexplained denial. A `Capability`-class ffmpeg failure writes a negative override; every override carries an expiry so a transient GPU fault does not permanently denylist `hevc_nvenc` on the only GPU agent in the cluster.

- `pub struct CapabilityOverride { pub requirement: Requirement, pub allowed: bool, pub reason: String, pub evidence: Option<String>, pub at_unix: i64, pub expires_unix: Option<i64> }` with `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize`, plus `pub fn is_active_at(&self, now_unix: i64) -> bool` (`expires_unix.is_none() || expires_unix > now_unix`).
- `pub struct OverrideSet(Vec<CapabilityOverride>)` with `new`, `push`, `iter`, `len`, `is_empty`, `FromIterator`, and `pub fn lookup(&self, req: &Requirement, now_unix: i64) -> Option<bool>` returning the `allowed` flag of the first ACTIVE override whose `requirement == *req`.
- `pub fn satisfies_with_overrides(cap: &Capability, req: &Requirements, overrides: &OverrideSet, now_unix: i64) -> Result<(), UnmetRequirement>` — for each requirement in order: if `lookup` returns `Some(false)`, fail immediately with `UnmetReason::Missing`; if `Some(true)`, treat as satisfied without consulting `cap`; if `None`, delegate to `satisfies_one`.

title: BucketKey: categorical-only requirement hash for dispatch partitioning
description:
Implement the requirement bucket key the dispatcher uses to cache an eligibility bitset per distinct requirement shape. The key must hash ONLY the categorical requirements; including per-file byte counts or paths would explode cardinality toward one bucket per job and collapse the matcher to O(queue). Observed target bucket count for this deployment is single digits.

Create `crates/transcodarr-core/src/capability/bucket.rs` with:
- `pub struct BucketKey(String)` — `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize`, `Display` rendering `b3:<64-hex>`, and `pub fn as_str(&self) -> &str`.
- `pub fn bucket_key(req: &Requirements) -> BucketKey` — build a canonical byte string from the categorical subset, then `blake3::hash`. Rules:
  - INCLUDED: `AgentClass`, `Encoder`, `Decoder`, `Muxer`, `PlatformIn`, `LabelEquals`.
  - EXCLUDED: `MinEffectiveCores`, `MinFreeBytes`, `MountCovers`.
  - Canonicalisation: render each included requirement with its `Display` impl, sort the resulting strings lexicographically, deduplicate, join with `\n`. Ordering of the input vector must therefore not affect the key.
  - The `match` inside `bucket_key` must be exhaustive over `Requirement` (no `_ =>` arm) so a future variant forces an explicit included/excluded decision.
- `pub fn categorical_requirements(req: &Requirements) -> Vec<&Requirement>` — the same partition, exposed for tests and for the server's diagnostics view.

Add `blake3` to `crates/transcodarr-core/Cargo.toml` dependencies (workspace-inherited: `blake3 = { workspace = true }`) if it is not already present, and add `mod bucket; pub use bucket::*;` to `capability/mod.rs`.

title: CapabilityHash: stable hash excluding volatile fields
description:
Implement the capability document hash the agent sends in `Hello` and the server stores in `agent.capability_hash`. It must change when the agent's real abilities change (a driver update dropping `hevc_nvenc`) and must NOT change on every heartbeat because free space moved.

title: Capability diff summary for capability-history rows
description:
Implement the human-readable one-line diff stored in `agent_capability_history.diff_summary` and shown on the agent detail page, so "the GPU node stopped taking work after a Windows Update" resolves to one line at 03:14.

Create `crates/transcodarr-core/src/capability/diff.rs` with:

```rust
pub fn diff_summary(prev: &Capability, next: &Capability) -> String;
```

Output is a comma-and-space-joined list of deterministic, lexicographically sorted tokens, empty string when the two capabilities hash identically (reuse `capability_hash` for the short-circuit). Token forms, emitted in this section order:
1. Encoders: `-hevc_nvenc`, `+av1_nvenc`.
2. Muxers: `-matroska`, `+mp4`.
3. Decoders: `-nvdec:av1:*:8`, `+nvdec:hevc:main10:10`, and for a status change `nvdec:h264:high:10 verified_ok->verified_soft_fallback`.
4. Classes: `-gpu`, `+cpu`.
5. Mounts (by `canonical_prefix`): `-mount:/mnt/bigdata`, `+mount:/mnt/bd`.
6. Versions: `ffmpeg 6.1->7.0`, `ffprobe 6.1->7.0`, `driver 550.54->560.35`, `platform linux->windows`.

Volatile fields (free bytes, effective cores, evidence, probed_at_unix) are never reported. Add `mod diff; pub use diff::*;` to `capability/mod.rs`.

If the root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` does not already carry `rusqlite = { version = "0.32", features = ["bundled","serde_json","blob","backup"] }`, `blake3 = "1"`, `thiserror = "2"`, `tempfile = "3"`, add them and bump the root Cargo.toml header version by a minor step. crates/transcodarr-store/Cargo.toml declares `name = "transcodarr-store"`, `edition.workspace = true`, `license.workspace = true`, deps rusqlite/blake3/thiserror (all `.workspace = true`), dev-dep tempfile. src/lib.rs carries `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, `#![warn(missing_docs)]`, a `//!` module doc, and `pub mod error; pub mod pragma;` plus `pub use error::StoreError;`. Note rusqlite `bundled` ships SQLite >= 3.44 so `STRICT` tables and partial indexes are available; do not add a system sqlite dependency. In-memory databases cannot enter WAL mode, so the pragma tests must use a file DB in a `tempfile::TempDir`.

title: Migrator, schema_migration table, and blake3 migration checksums
description: Add `src/migrate.rs` implementing the embedded migration runner, plus the shared integration-test helper module. The `schema_migration` table is bootstrapped by the migrator itself (DDL string constant in Rust, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migration (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, checksum TEXT NOT NULL, applied_unix INTEGER NOT NULL) STRICT;`) — it is deliberately NOT a .sql migration file. `MIGRATIONS` starts as an EMPTY slice in this task; tasks S7-003..S7-008 each append exactly one entry. Behaviour: `apply_all` iterates migrations in ascending version order, skips versions already recorded, verifies the stored checksum against `checksum(sql)` for already-applied versions and returns `ChecksumMismatch` on drift, rejects a non-contiguous version sequence, and executes each pending migration's SQL together with its `schema_migration` INSERT inside ONE transaction so a failed migration leaves no partial DDL. `checksum` returns `format!("b3:{}", blake3::hash(sql.as_bytes()).to_hex())` over the FULL file text including its header comment — therefore released migration files are immutable and their `-- version: 1.0.0` header must never be bumped; document this rule in the module `//!` doc. Also create `tests/common/mod.rs` with the helpers every later test file reuses.

title: Core scan identity + change classification types
description: Create the pure, I/O-free change-detection primitives the scanner depends on. This is the single concept: given what the DB already knows about a file and what a fresh stat(2) says, decide New / Changed / Unchanged / TooFresh. No filesystem access, no async, no rusqlite — this module must compile inside transcodarr-core which forbids all I/O crates. TooFresh implements B13 (never enqueue a file still being written): a file whose mtime is younger than min_mtime_age_s must be skipped this pass rather than upserted as changed, but an otherwise-unchanged file is reported Unchanged regardless of mtime age (touching a file must not make it invisible). Changed is true when size_bytes, mtime_unix, mtime_ns, or identity differ from stored. Identity is Option so non-unix platforms and stat failures degrade gracefully.

pub struct StatFacts { pub size_bytes: u64, pub mtime_unix: i64, pub mtime_ns: u32, pub identity: Option<FileIdentity> }
pub struct StoredScanRef { pub file_id: i64, pub size_bytes: u64, pub mtime_unix: i64, pub mtime_ns: u32, pub identity: Option<FileIdentity>, pub has_probe: bool }
#[non_exhaustive] pub enum ChangeKind { New, Changed, Unchanged, TooFresh }
pub fn classify_change(stored: Option<&StoredScanRef>, fresh: &StatFacts, now_unix: i64, min_mtime_age_s: i64) -> ChangeKind
acceptance: File `crates/transcodarr-core/src/scan/change.rs` begins with the 3-line header (`// file:` / `// version: 1.0.0` / `// guid: <new uuid>`) and `crates/transcodarr-core/src/lib.rs` declares `pub mod scan;`.

title: Core mass-missing abort guard
description: Pure guard (flaw B18) that refuses to mark a huge fraction of a library missing. The catastrophic case is an NFS mount that vanished mid-scan: the walk sees zero files, every one of 29,400 rows would flip to missing, and the next evaluation pass would treat the entire TV library as gone. Guard is deliberately two-sided: absolute floor so a small library deleting a handful of files is never blocked, and a ratio so a large library cannot lose more than max_missing_ratio in one run. Returning Err does NOT mean the scan failed — the caller aborts only the missing-marking step and records `scan_run.status='aborted'` with a reason.
apis: pub struct MassMissingPolicy { pub abs_floor: u64, pub max_missing_ratio: f64 }
impl Default for MassMissingPolicy // abs_floor = 50, max_missing_ratio = 0.10
#[non_exhaustive] pub struct MassMissingAbort { pub would_be_missing: u64, pub known_total: u64, pub ratio: f64 }
impl std::fmt::Display for MassMissingAbort
pub fn check_mass_missing(known_total: u64, would_be_missing: u64, policy: &MassMissingPolicy) -> Result<(), MassMissingAbort>

title: Server blocking library walker
description: The only filesystem-touching piece of S10. A synchronous, bounded walk of one library root that the caller runs under `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (R3: scanning must never occupy the dispatch runtime). Uses `walkdir` with `follow_links(false)` and `max_depth(cfg.max_depth)`, prunes excluded directories via `filter_entry` so `.zfs` is never descended, filters files by `cfg.is_media_extension`, and lifts `(dev, inode, nlink)` from `std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt` behind `#[cfg(unix)]` (yielding `identity: None` on other platforms). Per-entry errors (EACCES, ESTALE on a flaky NFS mount) are reported as `WalkEvent::Error` and the walk continues; only a failure to open the root itself is a hard `Err`. The sink returns `ControlFlow` so the caller can stop early on cancellation. This task performs NO database work and NO probing.
apis: pub struct DiscoveredFile { pub canonical_path: camino::Utf8PathBuf, pub facts: transcodarr_core::scan::StatFacts }
#[non_exhaustive] pub enum SkipReason { Excluded, NotMedia, NotAFile, Symlink, DepthExceeded }
#[non_exhaustive] pub enum WalkEvent { File(DiscoveredFile), Skipped { path: camino::Utf8PathBuf, reason: SkipReason }, Error { path: camino::Utf8PathBuf, message: String } }
pub struct WalkStats { pub files_yielded: u64, pub dirs_visited: u64, pub skipped: u64, pub errors: u64 }
pub fn walk_library(root: &camino::Utf8Path, cfg: &ScanConfig, exclude: &ExcludeSet, sink: &mut dyn FnMut(WalkEvent) -> std::ops::ControlFlow<()>) -> Result<WalkStats, WalkError>

title: Store: FileRepo::upsert_scanned (idempotent, probe-preserving)
description: The heart of S10 and the direct inversion of Tdarr failure mode 7 ('a fresh scan DROPS all existing records and re-probes from disk'). One function, three branches keyed on the `ChangeKind` the caller already computed. It must contain no DELETE and must never write NULL into `probe_json`. The Unchanged branch is deliberately the narrowest possible UPDATE — only `last_seen_unix` and `scan_generation` — because that is what makes a rescan of 29.4k unchanged files nearly free and guarantees stored probe data, decisions and skip markers survive. The Changed branch refreshes the stat facts, resets `state` to 'discovered' and clears `eval_rules_version` and `content_sig` so the file is re-probed and re-evaluated, but still leaves `probe_json` in place (the old probe is the fallback for the explain view until the new one lands). Critical schema interaction: `idx_file_ident` is UNIQUE on `(dev, inode)` where inode is not null, so a hardlinked file (nlink > 1) MUST be inserted with `dev`/`inode` written as NULL — otherwise the second link of a seeding torrent violates the unique index and aborts the scan.

impl FileRepo { pub fn upsert_scanned(&self, tx: &rusqlite::Transaction<'_>, change: ChangeKind, existing: Option<&ScannedFileRow>, u: &ScanUpsert<'_>) -> Result<ScanUpsertOutcome, StoreError>; }

title: Store: rename reconciliation via (dev, inode)
description: Handles the path-hash-miss / identity-hit case: the same inode appeared at a new path, i.e. the operator renamed or moved a file. Without this, a rename would attempt an INSERT that violates the UNIQUE `idx_file_ident` index, and even if it didn't it would orphan the old row and throw away a perfectly good probe. The fix is to move the existing row to the new path, preserving `probe_json`, `decision`, `eval_rules_version`, `bytes_reclaimed` and `first_seen_unix`. Only valid when `nlink == 1` — with nlink > 1 the identity is shared between two live paths and is not a rename, so the caller must fall through to a plain insert (which S10-007 already handles by writing NULL identity).

acceptance: Test `test_reconcile_rename_moves_row_and_preserves_probe` inserts a row with `probe_json`, `decision = 'video'` and `eval_rules_version = 'b3:xyz'`, calls `reconcile_rename` to a new path, and asserts: `canonical_path` and `path_hash` are the new values; `probe_json`, `decision`, `eval_rules_version`, `first_seen_unix` are all unchanged; `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM file` is still 1.

title: Scanner orchestrator wiring walk to store
description: Assembles the pieces into one library scan. Runs `walk_library` under `spawn_blocking` and streams `WalkEvent`s over a bounded channel (capacity = cfg.batch_size) so an 85TB walk cannot balloon memory or block the runtime. For each discovered file: compute `path_hash = blake3(canonical_path)`, `lookup_by_path_hash`; on miss `lookup_by_identity` and, when the hit has `nlink == 1`, call `reconcile_rename`; otherwise `classify_change` and `upsert_scanned`. Upserts are submitted to `Writer` in batches of `cfg.batch_size` on `WriteLane::Bulk`, one transaction per batch, with counters flushed via `update_counters` after each. After the walk completes: count stale rows, run `check_mass_missing`, and either call `mark_missing_by_generation` and `finish(Ok)`, or skip the sweep entirely and `finish(Aborted, reason)`. `ChangeKind::TooFresh` files increment `files_seen` only and are NOT upserted (their generation stays stale, so the guard must exclude them — bump their generation with a last_seen-only touch so a still-being-written file is never reported missing). This task does NO probing: new and changed rows are left in `state = 'discovered'` for the probe ingestor to pick up.

title: Permit delta derivation from state transitions
description: Encode the rule that permits are acquired on ENTERING the admitted set and released on LEAVING it - not on reaching a terminal state. This is the fix for the double-counted-capacity flaw: Running->Retrying releases even though Retrying is not terminal, and Assigned->Running / Verifying->Committing release nothing because both endpoints are admitted. Provide `pub enum PermitDelta { Acquire, Release, None }` (#[non_exhaustive], Copy/Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq) and `pub const fn permit_delta(from: JobState, to: JobState) -> PermitDelta` derived from `holds_permits()` on both endpoints: Acquire when !from.holds_permits() && to.holds_permits(); Release when from.holds_permits() && !to.holds_permits(); None otherwise. Also `pub enum ReleaseReason { Completed, Failed, Requeued, Cancelled, LeaseExpired, DeadLettered }` (#[non_exhaustive]) with `pub const fn release_reason_for(to: JobState) -> Option<ReleaseReason>` mapping Succeeded->Completed, Failed->Failed, NeedsOperator->Failed, Cancelled->Cancelled, DeadLettered->DeadLettered, Retrying->Requeued, Eligible->Requeued, Blocked->Requeued, and None for admitted destinations. Wire `pub mod permits;` into job/mod.rs (bump header to 1.4.0).

title: JobRepo::transition - compare-and-swap UPDATE plus job_event append
description: Implement the single mutation path for job state. Signature: `pub fn transition(&self, tx: &rusqlite::Transaction<'_>, t: &Transition) -> Result<(), TransitionError>`. Behaviour, in order: (1) if `!JobState::can_transition(t.from, t.to)` return Illegal without touching the DB; (2) execute the CAS `UPDATE job SET state=:to, updated_unix=:now, agent_id=COALESCE(:agent_id, agent_id), attempt=:attempt, lease_expires_unix=:lease, not_before_unix=COALESCE(:not_before, not_before_unix), terminal_reason=:terminal_reason, finished_unix=CASE WHEN :is_terminal THEN :now ELSE finished_unix END, started_unix=CASE WHEN :to='Running' AND started_unix IS NULL THEN :now ELSE started_unix END WHERE id=:job_id AND state=:from`; (3) if rows_affected == 0, re-SELECT the current state and return `Lost { expected: t.from, actual }` (or `Store` if the row vanished); (4) on success INSERT the job_event row (job_id, at_unix_ms, from_state, to_state, agent_id, attempt, reason_code, detail) in the same transaction. Timestamps: job.updated_unix/finished_unix/started_unix are SECONDS (t.at_unix_ms / 1000); job_event.at_unix_ms is millis. Use named parameters, never string formatting. No .await, no logging to a slow sink, no other side effects - permit accounting is the caller's job via core::permit_delta.

title: Transition guards: terminal immutability and fencing-epoch staleness
description: Harden JobRepo::transition with the two guards that protect against a stale agent completing work the server has already reassigned. (1) Terminal immutability: before the CAS, if `t.from.is_terminal()` return `TerminalImmutable { state: t.from }`; additionally the CAS WHERE clause must already prevent updating a row that is terminal in the DB, and a Lost error whose `actual` is terminal must be reported as TerminalImmutable instead of Lost so callers can distinguish 'someone beat me' from 'this row is frozen forever'. (2) Fencing: when `t.fencing_epoch` is Some(e), add `AND (fencing_epoch IS NULL OR fencing_epoch = :epoch)` to the CAS predicate; when rows_affected == 0 and the row's state still equals t.from, re-read fencing_epoch and return `FencingStale { expected: e, got: actual }` rather than Lost. Also add a defensive DB-level guard: a SQLite trigger `trg_job_terminal_immutable` in a small follow-on migration that raises ABORT on any UPDATE of a job row whose OLD.state is terminal and whose NEW values differ, so a future code path that bypasses JobRepo cannot silently mutate history. Bump the transition.rs header version.

title: CpuQuotaReader: cgroup v2 effective cores
description: Derive `effective_cores` (R34) from cgroup v2, honouring the systemd CPUQuota used on U1 for thermal control. `parse_cpu_max` handles the two-token cpu.max format: "max 100000" -> None (unlimited), "1200000 100000" -> Some(12.0). `parse_self_cgroup` extracts the relative path from a /proc/self/cgroup line like "0::/system.slice/transcodarr-agent.service". `effective_cores()` walks the ancestor chain from the agent's own cgroup path up to the root, collecting every non-`max` quota, and returns the MINIMUM of those quotas; if none is found it falls back to `std::thread::available_parallelism()` as f64, and to 1.0 if that also fails. title: Trial-decode result classification (pure)
description: The single most correctness-critical function in S14, and it is pure so it needs no ffmpeg. Maps a finished trial-decode run to a `DecoderStatus` plus a human-readable evidence string. Rule order is load-bearing and must be exactly: (1) `signal` is Some -> VerifiedFail, evidence "killed by signal N"; (2) exit_code != Some(0) -> VerifiedFail, evidence "exit N: <last stderr line>" (this is the measured Turing AV1 case: exit 69, 1KB truncated output); (3) exit 0 but stderr contains any marker in HWACCEL_INIT_FAILURE_MARKERS -> VerifiedSoftFallback, evidence "stderr: <matched marker line>" (the measured Turing Hi10 H.264 case: ffmpeg exits 0 having silently decoded on CPU while occupying a GPU slot); (4) exit 0, clean stderr, but frames_decoded is None or < expected_frames -> VerifiedFail, evidence "decoded X of Y frames"; (5) otherwise VerifiedOk. Step 3 MUST precede step 4 because a soft fallback also decodes all frames. Markers must cover both British and American spellings plus "Failed setup for format cuda", matched case-insensitively. Also provide `parse_frames_decoded` reading the LAST `frame=<N>` line from `-progress pipe:1` stdout.

title: Trial sample corpus generation
description: Produce the tiny synthetic clips the trial decodes run against, so probing needs no library media and no LFS fixtures. `encode_sample_argv` builds a deterministic lavfi encode: `-hide_banner -nostdin -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=320x240:rate=10:duration=1 -frames:v 10 -pix_fmt <yuv420p|yuv420p10le> -c:v <encoder> -y <out>`, choosing the software encoder per codec (h264->libx264, hevc->libx265, av1->libaom-av1, vp9->libvpx-vp9, mpeg2video->mpeg2video, vc1-> None) and returning None when no encoder is known or when the encoder is absent from the advertised set. `TrialSampleSet::ensure` is IDEMPOTENT per the repo's check-before-doing rule: for each requested key it skips generation when the file already exists and is larger than 1024 bytes; otherwise it encodes into `<dir>/<codec>_<bit_depth>.mkv` via a temp path + rename. title: TrialDecode runner
description: Execute one trial decode per triple and produce a `DecoderCapability`. `decode_argv` builds: `-hide_banner -nostdin <hwaccel_args_for(kind)> -i <sample> -map 0:v:0 -f null - -progress pipe:1 -v error` — argv vector only, never a shell string. `run_one` executes it with the configured timeout, feeds exit code/signal/stdout/stderr plus TRIAL_SAMPLE_FRAMES into `classify_trial`, and returns `DecoderCapability { triple, status, evidence, probed_at_unix }`. title: Probe fingerprint and on-disk capability cache
description: Implement 'Re-probes on binary or driver change'. `ProbeFingerprint` captures PROBE_SCHEMA_VERSION plus the ffmpeg binary path/size/mtime_ns, the ffmpeg and ffprobe version strings, the nvidia driver version, and the agent version; `hash()` is blake3 over those fields joined with a NUL separator in a fixed order, rendered as "b3:<hex>". The cache is a JSON file at `<state_dir>/capability.json` holding {fingerprint_hash, capability, probed_at_unix}. `store` writes to `<path>.tmp`, fsyncs the file, renames, then fsyncs the parent dir — a torn cache must never be readable. `load` returns None (never Err) on missing file, malformed JSON, or a schema mismatch, so a corrupt cache degrades to a full re-probe rather than a startup failure. `needs_reprobe` returns true when the cache is absent or its `fingerprint_hash` differs from the current fingerprint's hash.

title: Capability document assembly and capability_hash
description: Assemble the full `Capability` document that Register/Hello send, and hash it. `CapabilityProber::fingerprint()` runs `ffmpeg -version`, `ffprobe -version` and the driver probe and stats the ffmpeg binary. `probe(mode, mounts)` does: fingerprint -> if mode==Cached and !needs_reprobe, return the cached Capability unchanged (per the protocol contract, a reconnect within the same process resends the cached document and the hash proves it); otherwise run `-encoders`/`-decoders`/`-hwaccels`, derive triples, ensure samples, run trial decodes, read effective/physical cores, assemble, hash, store the cache, return. `derive_classes` yields sorted class labels: "cpu" always; "audio" when the eac3 encoder is advertised; "gpu" only when at least one non-Software decoder is VerifiedOk AND a `*_nvenc` encoder is advertised — a SoftFallback-only GPU is NOT a gpu-class agent. `capability_hash` is blake3 over the canonical JSON of the document with the `capability_hash` field itself emptied and all collections sorted, so it is order-independent and self-consistent. Mounts are passed in by the caller (mount/rename probing is a separate subsystem) and are sorted by canonical_prefix before hashing.

title: Agent runtime wiring: reprobe triggers and CapabilityUpdate
description: Wire the prober into the agent runtime created by S12. Three integration points, no new probing logic. (1) Startup/registration: call `probe(ProbeMode::Cached, mounts)` before `Register`; a brand-new boot_id with no matching cache runs full trial decodes, a reconnect within the same process resends the cached document. (2) `ServerMessage::ReprobeCapabilities{force_trial_decodes}`: run `probe` with ForceTrialDecodes when the flag is set (Cached otherwise) on a spawned task so the stream pump is never blocked by a multi-second probe, then send `AgentMessage::CapabilityUpdate{capability, change_summary}` on the LOSSLESS outbound lane, computing change_summary via `capability_diff` against the previously held document. (3) A `fingerprint_watch` interval task (default 15 minutes, configurable) that recomputes only the fingerprint (cheap: two -version calls plus a stat) and triggers an automatic reprobe + CapabilityUpdate when the hash changed — this is what catches a Windows-side driver update. Additionally, the heartbeat builder must call `CpuQuotaReader::effective_cores()` on EVERY beat rather than reusing the registration value, so a live systemd CPUQuota change is reflected within one 5s beat. The current Capability is held in an `arc_swap::ArcSwap` so heartbeats and reprobes never block one another.
apis: impl AgentRuntime { pub fn current_capability(&self) -> std::sync::Arc<transcodarr_core::Capability>; pub async fn reprobe(&self, mode: ProbeMode) -> Result<(transcodarr_core::Capability, String), ProbeError>; pub fn spawn_fingerprint_watch(self: std::sync::Arc<Self>, interval: std::time::Duration) -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>; }

title: Match predicate evaluation with first-failing-predicate reporting
description: Implement `Match::check(&self, facts: &FileFacts) -> Result<(), PredicateFailure>` — pure, no I/O, no allocation of the whole facts. Predicates are AND-ed and evaluated in the declared field order; the FIRST failing predicate is returned so `evaluate_explained` can report it. Exact semantics (all string comparisons are ASCII-case-insensitive, all list membership is `contains`): library_in -> facts.library_name in list; container_in -> facts.container in list; video_codec_in -> facts.video_codec in list; video_codec_not_in -> facts.video_codec NOT in list (a file with no video stream fails video_codec_in and passes video_codec_not_in); video_bit_depth_in -> facts.video_bit_depth in list; hdr/dovi/has_object_audio -> exact bool equality; dovi_profile_in -> facts.dovi_profile is Some(p) and p in list (None fails); min_width/max_width -> inclusive bounds on facts.video_width (None width fails either bound); min_size_bytes/max_size_bytes -> inclusive on facts.size_bytes; min_duration_s -> facts.duration_s >= value (None duration fails); audio_codec_any_in -> ANY audio track codec is in the list; max_audio_channels -> the MAXIMUM channel count over audio tracks is <= value; nlink_min -> facts.nlink >= value; nlink_max -> facts.nlink <= value. path_glob is handled in S4-006 and must be the LAST predicate checked (leave a `todo`-free stub returning Ok until then, wired in S4-006). Do NOT touch the filesystem for path_glob or anything else.

impl std::fmt::Display for PredicateFailure // renders `hdr = true (actual false)`

title: Audio track selection: per-stream eligibility, bitrate and over-6-channel policy
description: Implement the pure per-track audio logic that turns an AudioPlan template plus the file's audio streams into a concrete stream selection. Rules, in order, per audio stream: (1) if the stream's codec is in `defaults.leave_alone`, exclude with reason `LeaveAlone`; (2) if the codec is NOT in `plan.match_codecs`, exclude with reason `CodecNotMatched`; (3) if `channels > 6`, apply `plan.over_6_channels` — Skip -> exclude with reason `ChannelsExceedEac3`, KeepOriginal -> exclude with reason `KeepOriginal`, Downmix -> include with the bitrate for 6 channels; (4) otherwise include. Bitrate lookup is deterministic: the value for the GREATEST key in `bitrate_by_channels` that is <= the stream's channel count; if no such key exists, the value for the SMALLEST key. All codec comparisons are ASCII-case-insensitive. If S1's `FileFacts` does not already expose per-stream audio facts, add the minimal `pub audio_streams: Vec<AudioStreamFacts>` ({ index: u32, codec: String, channels: u16 }) to it as part of this task.

title: evaluate_explained engine and evaluate wrapper
description: Implement the ordered rule fold. Signature: `evaluate_explained(&FileFacts, &Policy) -> (Decision, Vec<RuleTrace>)`, with `evaluate` a thin wrapper returning only the Decision. Semantics, exactly: iterate `policy.rule` in order; call `Match::check`; push a RuleTrace for EVERY rule (matched true/false, `failed_predicate` = the Display of the PredicateFailure when unmatched). On a match, apply the action — EncodeAudio: if the audio stage is blocked or `decision.audio.is_some()`, trace `applied=false, skipped_reason="stage_already_planned"|"stage_blocked"`; else run `select_audio_streams`, and if the selection is empty push `BlockedStage{Audio, "no_eligible_audio_streams", Some(rule)}` and leave audio None, otherwise set `decision.audio` with `streams` filled from the selection. EncodeVideo: same guard logic; resolve `pix_fmt = pix_fmt_for(encoder_preference[0], facts.video_bit_depth)` (S1 function) and store it. SkipVideo: set video None, push `BlockedStage{Video, reason, Some(rule)}`, mark the video stage blocked. Skip: block BOTH stages with the given reason, clear both plans. Quarantine: set `decision.quarantine`, clear both plans, block both stages. After applying, if `rule.stops()` break out of the loop and mark all remaining rules as untraced (do not push traces for rules never reached — but DO push a final trace-less state; document this). Finally set `decision.class = DecisionClass::from_plans(...)` and build `decision.reason` as the semicolon-joined list of contributions in application order, where an applied encode contributes `rule <name>` and a block contributes its `reason` string; an empty list yields `"no_rule_matched"`. The function must be pure: no filesystem access, no clock, no RNG, no global state.

title: Skip-marker suppression: apply_skip_markers
description: Pure helper the Evaluator uses to drop plans whose decision class already carries a live `file_skip_marker` at the CURRENT rules_version. title: LaneQueue: three-lane priority queue with single-lane batching and anti-starvation
description: The priority multiplexer between submitters and the writer thread. Backed by three VecDeques under one Mutex plus a Condvar, so it is a pure synchronous structure testable without a database or a runtime. The critical design property, which must be enforced and tested: a returned batch contains requests from EXACTLY ONE lane, so the writer can set the synchronous pragma once per batch rather than per op. Anti-starvation: after `starvation_every_n` consecutive batches drawn from higher-priority lanes, the next batch is forcibly drawn from the lowest non-empty lane, so a sustained Commit stream cannot permanently block Bulk retention work.

title: Fsync latency probe with hard-abort budget enforcement

title: ReadPool: r2d2 read-only connection pool with per-connection pragma re-assert
description: The API and UI read path. An r2d2 pool of read-only SQLite connections opened against the same WAL database the writer owns, so reads never contend with the single writer. title: WriterActor loop: grouped commit with per-op SAVEPOINT isolation
description: The heart of S8. A dedicated OS thread owning the single write connection, pulling one single-lane batch at a time from LaneQueue and committing the whole batch in one transaction — this is what makes SQLite's single writer fast enough for 30+ concurrent jobs, versus nedb's fsync-per-write pathology. Within the batch each op runs inside its own SAVEPOINT so one failing op rolls back only itself and its peers still commit. The synchronous pragma is set once per batch from `lane.synchronous()` and only when it differs from the current setting, so Commit-lane batches get FULL durability while Bulk retention work stays on NORMAL. Panic handling and commit-failure replay are deliberately NOT in this task (see S8-007); here a failing op is one that returns Err.

title: Poison quarantine: panic containment, commit-failure isolation replay, bounded ledger
description: Make one bad op unable to kill the writer thread or take a whole batch down with it. Two mechanisms. (1) Panic containment: each op runs inside `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))`; a panic rolls back that savepoint only, replies `WriterPoisoned`, records the op name in the ledger, and the writer thread continues serving. (2) Isolation replay: if the batch `COMMIT` itself fails (e.g. a deferred FK violation that only surfaces at commit), the batch is rolled back and every request is re-run alone in its own transaction; whichever request still fails is quarantined — replied to with an error, recorded, and never retried again — while the innocent ones commit. The ledger is a bounded ring so a pathological loop cannot exhaust memory, and its contents feed `transcodarr admin fsck` diagnostics.

Repo root is /home/jdfalk/repos/github/jdfalk/transcodarr; all paths below are repo-relative and every new file needs the 3-line `// file: / // version: 1.0.0 / // guid: <new uuid>` header.

This is the single place that decides how probe JSON becomes queryable columns, and it is reused later by the job-completion probe write-through path (R11), so it must not depend on the scanner.

Rules the mapping must implement:
- `audio_codecs` is a sorted, deduplicated, comma-separated string built from audio stream codec names (e.g. `"eac3,truehd"`).
- `audio_track_count` / `subtitle_track_count` count ALL such streams, not just the default one.
- `video_bit_depth` and `video_pix_fmt` come from the first video stream verbatim; 8-bit must stay 8 and 10-bit must stay 10 (no normalisation, no defaulting to 8 when the field is present).
- `is_hdr` is true when `color_transfer` is `smpte2084` or `arib-std-b67`, OR `color_primaries` is `bt2020`.
- `is_dovi` is true when the video stream carries `DOVI configuration record` side data; `dovi_profile` is that record's `dv_profile` when present, else `None`.
- `has_object_audio` is true when any audio stream profile contains `Atmos` or `DTS:X` (case-insensitive).
- `audio_bytes` = sum over audio streams of `bit_rate_bps * duration_s / 8`, rounded down; `None` when no audio stream reports a bit rate.
- `size_bucket` via `transcodarr_core::size_bucket_for(size_bytes, thresholds)`.
- `content_sig` via `transcodarr_core::content_sig(&derive_facts(probe, size_bytes))`.
- `probe_json` is the raw JSON string passed in, stored verbatim (never re-serialised).

Enums carried in `StreamRow.kind` must serialise to the exact CHECK spellings in the schema: `video|audio|subtitle|attachment|data`.

Add unit tests using small inline JSON fixtures (no media files, no network).

stdout is captured (piped, not inherited) and parsed with `transcodarr_core::parse_ffprobe_json`. stderr is captured and its last 8 KiB retained on failure. A child exceeding `timeout` is killed and reported as `ProbeError::Timeout`.

`tool_version` runs `<ffprobe_path> -version` once and returns the first line, cached by the caller.

Use `#[non_exhaustive]` on the error enum and `thiserror` for it (library-layer error style per rust.instructions.md).

title: Prober task: bounded-concurrency probe loop with write-through
description:
The task that walks probe candidates for one library and turns them into stored facts. Only new or changed files are touched — the candidate query (S11-003) is the sole definition of 'needs probing'; this task never re-probes an already-probed unchanged file.

Loop shape: page candidates via `next_probe_batch` on a `spawn_blocking` read, run at most `cfg.max_concurrency` concurrent `ProbeSource::probe` calls (`tokio::sync::Semaphore` or `buffer_unordered`), and for each result submit `WriteOp::ProbeWriteThrough` (success) or `WriteOp::ProbeFailed` (error) on `WriteLane::Bulk`. A probe failure must never abort the pass. Missing files (`ProbeError::Spawn` with `NotFound`, or a path that no longer exists) increment `skipped_missing` and are recorded as probe_failed.

Size for the write-through comes from the candidate row's `size_bytes` (already stat'd by the scanner), so the prober performs no `stat` of its own.

Metrics: increment `transcodarr_scan_files_total{library, result}` with result in `{"probed","error"}`. If a `scan_run_id` is supplied, accumulate into `scan_run.probe_errors` at the end of the pass via one write op.

Keep the module under ~250 lines; the ffprobe mechanics live in S11-004 and the SQL in S11-002/003.

title: FileRepo::next_eval_batch keyset loader hydrating FileFacts from columns only

title: LibraryRoundRobin cursor for fair batch interleaving
description:
Pure data structure, no I/O, no async. Prevents the 29.4k-file TV library from monopolising evaluation ahead of the 2.4k-file movie library by handing out one batch cursor per library in rotation.

Semantics:
- `new(libraries)` seeds every library as active with `after = None`.
- `next()` returns the next active library's cursor in round-robin order, or `None` when no library is active.
- `advance(library_id, last_seen, returned, limit)`: if `returned < limit as usize`, the library is marked exhausted for this pass and is skipped by future `next()` calls; otherwise its cursor advances to `after = last_seen` and it stays active.
- `reset()` reactivates every library and clears all cursors (used at the start of a new pass).
- `active_len()` reports how many libraries remain active.

Order must be deterministic (insertion order) so tests can assert on interleaving.

pub struct LibraryRoundRobin { /* private */ }

title: Skip-marker suppression and policy-convergence guard (pure)
description:
Two pure functions applied to a `Decision` after `transcodarr_core::evaluate` returns, before it is persisted. No I/O, no async.

`suppress_marked`: drops the audio half of a Decision when a live `('audio', current_rules_version)` marker exists, and the video half when a `('video', current_rules_version)` marker exists. Markers whose `rules_version` differs from the current one are ignored entirely (a policy change invalidates all markers by construction). This is flaw A3's fix: a video no-gain marker must NOT suppress a legitimate later Opus->EAC3 audio pass on the same file. After suppression, recompute `Decision::class` from which plans survive (None / Audio / Video / AudioThenVideo) and append the suppression reason(s) to `Decision::reason`.

`convergence`: implements the anti-livelock guard. If the previously completed decision class is repeated by the new decision under the same rules_version, the streak increments; at streak >= 2 return `Convergence::Quarantine { reason: "PolicyNotConverging", streak }`. If the class is not repeated, the streak resets to 0. A rules_version change always resets the streak to 0 and returns Ok.
apis: #[derive(Debug, Clone)] pub struct SkipMarker { pub decision_class: DecisionClass, pub rules_version: RulesVersion, pub reason: String }
pub fn suppress_marked(decision: Decision, markers: &[SkipMarker], current: &RulesVersion) -> Decision
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum Convergence { Ok { streak: u32 }, Quarantine { reason: &'static str, streak: u32 } }
pub fn convergence(prev_streak: u32, prev_decision: Option<DecisionClass>, prev_rules: Option<&RulesVersion>, next: &Decision, current: &RulesVersion) -> Convergence

`test_convergence_quarantines_at_streak_two` passes: prev_streak = 1 with a repeated class returns Quarantine { reason: "PolicyNotConverging", streak: 2 }.
`test_convergence_resets_when_class_not_repeated` passes: returns Ok { streak: 0 }.
`test_convergence_resets_on_rules_version_change` passes: prev_streak = 1, repeated class, but prev_rules != current returns Ok { streak: 0 }.

title: FileRepo::apply_evaluations batched decision persistence
description:
Write a whole evaluation batch to the `file` table in one transaction using one reused prepared statement. This is the only place evaluation results are persisted.

Per row: `UPDATE file SET decision = ?, decision_reason = ?, eval_rules_version = ?, eval_at_unix = ?, content_sig = ?, same_decision_streak = ?, state = ?, quarantine_reason = ? WHERE id = ?`.

State mapping the caller supplies and the repo validates against the schema CHECK list: a decision of `none` pairs with state `processed`; any actionable decision pairs with state `evaluated`; a convergence quarantine pairs with state `quarantined` and a non-empty quarantine_reason. Reject the batch with `StoreError::Invalid` if a row violates that pairing — an inconsistent pair is a caller bug, not something to silently store.

The entire batch is atomic: any failure rolls back all rows. Expose `WriteOp::ApplyEvaluations(Vec<EvaluationOutcome>)` on `WriteLane::Bulk`. Do not touch probe columns, `file_stream`, or job rows.

enum WriteOp { ApplyEvaluations(Vec<EvaluationOutcome>), /* existing variants */ }

title: Evaluator task: batched pass over dirty files with library round-robin
description:
Wire S11-006..009 into the Evaluator. This task writes glue plus metrics; it must not contain SQL, decision logic, or job creation.

`run_pass` drains every dirty file exactly once: reset the round-robin, then loop { cursor = rr.next() or break; rows = spawn_blocking(next_eval_batch(cursor, batch_size)); for each row -> core::evaluate(&facts, &policy) -> suppress_marked(...) -> convergence(...) -> EvaluationOutcome; submit one WriteOp::ApplyEvaluations per batch; rr.advance(...) }.

Hard constraints:
- Zero filesystem I/O and zero ffprobe. The `evaluator` module must not reference `std::fs`, `std::process`, `tokio::fs` or `tokio::process`. Enforce this with a test that greps the module's own source files.
- The active policy is read once per pass from `ArcSwap<Policy>` so a mid-pass config swap cannot produce a batch evaluated under two rules versions.
- Skip markers for the batch are loaded in the same spawn_blocking call as the batch (one extra query per batch, keyed `file_id IN (...)`).
- Job creation is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the Planner (separate subsystem) consumes `idx_file_dispatchable`. This task only writes decisions.

Metrics: observe `transcodarr_policy_eval_duration_seconds` once per pass; set `transcodarr_policy_rules_version_info{hash}` to 1 for the active version. Register descriptions in `describe_all()`.

`run` loops `run_pass` on `cfg.idle_poll`, exits cleanly on the shutdown token, and never panics on a StoreError (log at warn, back off, retry).

#[derive(Debug, Default)] pub struct EvalPassStats { pub evaluated: u64, pub quarantined: u64, pub by_class: std::collections::BTreeMap<DecisionClass, u64>, pub duration: std::time::Duration }

title: Dry-run policy diff: DiffAccumulator plus non-persisting evaluation sweep
description:
Backs `POST /api/v1/config/validate?diff=true`. Evaluates a candidate policy against all stored facts and reports the blast radius WITHOUT writing anything.

`DiffAccumulator` is pure: `observe(before, after, size_bytes, size_bucket)` increments either `unchanged` (when before == after) or the transition counter keyed `"<before>-><after>"` using the snake_case DecisionClass spellings from the schema (`none`, `audio`, `video`, `audio_then_video`), e.g. `"none->audio"`. Actionable results (after != None) also add to `jobs_created`, add `size_bytes` to `estimated_input_bytes`, and add to `large_bucket_jobs` when `size_bucket == SizeBucket::Large`.

`dry_run_diff` streams every file (all libraries, ignoring `eval_rules_version`, so a candidate policy is measured against the whole library — use a dedicated `SQL_DIFF_BATCH` variant of the eval batch query without the `eval_rules_version IS NULL` predicate, still keyset paged and still never reading probe_json), evaluates each with `transcodarr_core::evaluate` under the candidate policy, applies `suppress_marked` with the candidate's `rules_version` (so all existing markers are correctly ignored), and observes the transition against the file's currently stored `decision`. It opens only read connections, submits zero WriteOps, and records `eval_duration_ms`.

impl FileRepo { pub fn next_diff_batch(&self, conn: &rusqlite::Connection, after: Option<FileId>, limit: u32) -> Result<Vec<EvalRow>, StoreError> }

title: Intent journal record types (IntentPhase, IntentId, IntentRecord)
description: Define the serde types the journal and the crash-matrix resolver both read. Pure data, no I/O. `IntentPhase` is the three-valued phase marker from the commit ritual; `IntentRecord` is exactly what gets fsynced to $STATE_DIR/intents/<intent_id>.json before each destructive step. `with_phase` returns a copy with the phase advanced and `updated_unix_ms` refreshed — it must never mutate in place, so a partially written successor cannot corrupt the predecessor in memory.

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct IntentId(pub u64);
impl std::fmt::Display for IntentId

impl IntentRecord { pub fn with_phase(&self, phase: IntentPhase, now_unix_ms: u64) -> Self; pub fn file_name(&self) -> String; pub fn is_owned_by(&self, agent_uid: &str, boot_id: &str) -> bool; }

title: fsops core: fsync, stat identity, hard link, and DestructiveAuthorization
description: The single module in the workspace permitted to call rename/remove_file/remove_dir_all on a media path. `DestructiveAuthorization` is an unforgeable token with private fields and exactly two constructors: one from a journal record already at IntentPhase::Granted or later, and one scoped to this agent's own work-area namespace (agent_uid + boot_id). Destructive functions take `&DestructiveAuthorization` so a future refactor cannot add a stray delete path. `hard_link` is idempotent: EEXIST whose destination inode equals the source inode returns `LinkOutcome::AlreadyLinked`, EEXIST with a different inode is an error. `write_atomic` is for journal files only (temp sibling + fsync + rename + fsync dir) and needs no auth because it never touches a media path.
apis: #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct DestructiveAuthorization { /* private */ }

title: CI containment test: destructive fs calls only inside fsops
description: A mechanical lint expressed as a test, per the architecture's 'CI grep test over the workspace fails the build on any other call site'. Walk every *.rs file under crates/ (excluding crates/transcodarr-agent/src/fsops/ and any path segment named `tests` or `benches`), read it, and fail if it contains `fs::rename`, `fs::remove_file`, `fs::remove_dir_all`, `rename(` preceded by `std::fs::`, or `tokio::fs::rename`. The failure message must list every offending file:line so the fix is obvious. Use walkdir or a hand-rolled recursion; do not shell out to grep.

title: IntentJournal: durable phase-marked record store
description: Persist IntentRecords under <state_dir>/intents/<intent_id>.json so a crash at any ritual step is recoverable. Every `record` call must be crash-atomic and durable: serialize, `fsops::write_atomic`, then `fsops::fsync_dir` on the intents directory. `list` tolerates a torn or foreign file by skipping it and returning the count of skipped entries alongside the records — a single bad file must never prevent replay of the others. `scoped` filters to records owned by this agent_uid+boot_id, which is what gets sent as `live_intents` in RegisterRequest. Removal goes through fsops with a work-area authorization.

title: fsops::attrs — read and apply ownership, mode, and xattrs
description: Step S1 of the ritual copies uid/gid/mode and extended attributes from the source onto the temp so the installed replacement is indistinguishable from the original to Plex/Jellyfin and to the NFS export. `apply_attrs` must be a no-op-and-succeed when the target's uid/gid already match (the common non-root case) and must return an error when a genuine chown is required and fails — silently landing a file owned by the wrong user is a real operational failure. xattr support is unix-only behind cfg; on other platforms `read_attrs` returns an empty xattr vec and `apply_attrs` skips them.
apis: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)] pub struct SourceAttrs { pub uid: u32, pub gid: u32, pub mode: u32, pub xattrs: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)> }
pub fn read_attrs(path: &camino::Utf8Path) -> Result<SourceAttrs, FsError>;
pub fn apply_attrs(path: &camino::Utf8Path, attrs: &SourceAttrs) -> Result<(), FsError>;

Unit test `test_apply_attrs_skips_chown_when_uid_and_gid_already_match` asserts Ok for a same-owner target while running as a non-root user.

title: fsops::space — free-byte query, same-device check, and the pure admits() rule
description: The space half of preflight. `free_bytes` uses rustix::fs::statvfs (f_bavail * f_frsize) so it reports space available to a non-root user, not the root-reserved total. `same_device` compares st_dev of two existing paths, resolving to the nearest existing ancestor when the leaf does not yet exist (the temp output usually does not exist at preflight time) — this is what makes `BlockStage::WorkAreaCrossDevice` a dispatch/preflight verdict rather than an EXDEV surprise at rename time. `admits` is a pure saturating-arithmetic function with no I/O so it can be exhaustively unit tested.
apis: pub fn free_bytes(path: &camino::Utf8Path) -> Result<u64, FsError>;
pub fn device_of(path: &camino::Utf8Path) -> Result<u64, FsError>;
pub fn same_device(a: &camino::Utf8Path, b: &camino::Utf8Path) -> Result<bool, FsError>;
pub const fn admits(free_bytes: u64, reserve_bytes: u64, projected_bytes: u64) -> bool;

title: RenameProbe: prove rename-over-an-open-destination is atomic on this mount
description: Sets agent.commit_eligible. Create a destination file with known content A and KEEP A READ HANDLE OPEN on it; create a source file with content B; rename source over destination; then assert three things: the path now stat()s to the source's original inode, reading through the still-open handle still yields content A (proving the old inode survived rather than being truncated in place), and reading the path fresh yields B. Any EXDEV, permission error, or inode mismatch yields `NotAtomic { reason }`. Windows/WSL2 is the reason this exists — a mount where rename is emulated as copy+unlink must never be handed commit-bearing work. Clean up all probe files on every exit path, including failures.
apis: #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] pub enum RenameProbeStatus { Untested, AtomicVerified, NotAtomic { reason: String } }
impl RenameProbeStatus { pub fn is_commit_eligible(&self) -> bool; pub fn as_label(&self) -> &'static str; }
pub struct RenameProbe;
impl RenameProbe { pub fn run(dir: &camino::Utf8Path) -> RenameProbeStatus; }
acceptance: Unit test `test_rename_probe_on_tempdir_reports_atomic_verified` asserts `RenameProbeStatus::AtomicVerified` on a normal tmpfs/ext4/zfs TempDir.
Unit test `test_rename_probe_leaves_no_files_behind` asserts the probe directory is empty (0 entries) after a successful run.

Unit test `test_rename_probe_on_readonly_dir_reports_not_atomic` chmods a dir to 0o555 and asserts `NotAtomic` with a non-empty reason; skips with `eprintln!("SKIP: running as root"); return;` when euid is 0.
Unit test `test_rename_probe_status_is_commit_eligible_only_for_atomic_verified` covers all three variants.
The probe holds the destination handle open across the rename (verifiable by reading pre-rename content through it) — asserted inside `test_rename_probe_on_tempdir_reports_atomic_verified`.

title: SourceFingerprint: capture, verify, and the hardlink guard
description: The defence against replacing a file that changed underneath us between plan time and rename time. `capture` snapshots dev/inode/size/mtime_ns/nlink. `verify` compares field by field and returns the FIRST differing field by name so the operator sees `mtime_ns` rather than 'source changed'. `nlink_ok` is the hardlink guard: nlink > 1 means the source is hard-linked (a seeding torrent), and replacing it would break the other link and silently double pool usage, so such files are refused. Pure comparison logic must be testable without touching a filesystem, so `verify` takes two fingerprints rather than a path.
apis: #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct SourceFingerprint { pub dev: u64, pub inode: u64, pub size: u64, pub mtime_ns: i128, pub nlink: u64 }

impl SourceFingerprint { pub fn capture(path: &camino::Utf8Path) -> Result<Self, crate::fsops::FsError>; pub fn from_ident(ident: &crate::fsops::FileIdent) -> Self; pub fn verify(&self, actual: &Self) -> Result<(), SourceChanged>; pub const fn nlink_ok(&self) -> bool; }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)] #[error("source changed: {field} expected {expected} actual {actual}")] pub struct SourceChanged { pub field: &'static str, pub expected: String, pub actual: String }
acceptance: Unit test `test_fingerprint_verify_identical_returns_ok`.
Unit test `test_fingerprint_verify_reports_inode_field_first_when_inode_and_size_both_differ` asserts `field == "inode"`.
Unit test `test_fingerprint_verify_detects_mtime_ns_change_with_identical_size` (the case a size-only check misses).
Unit test `test_fingerprint_nlink_ok_false_when_nlink_is_two`.
Unit test `test_fingerprint_capture_after_hard_link_reports_nlink_two` uses a TempDir and `fsops::hard_link`.
`verify` returns `&'static str` field names drawn from a fixed set; no format-string field names.

title: AtomicReplacer::install — the single rename, guarded and verified
description: Step S4, isolated so it can be tested on its own. Given a DestructiveAuthorization, a temp path and a final path: assert both are on the same device (return CommitError::CrossDevice otherwise, never attempt the rename), perform exactly ONE fsops::rename_replace, fsync the containing directory, then stat the final path and return its dev/inode. There is no second rename and no window in which final_path does not exist. If the post-rename stat shows an inode that is neither the temp's pre-rename inode nor a plausible successor, return CommitError::InstallUnverified — on NFS this has lied before.

title: TrashCan: idempotent retire-by-hard-link of the original
description: Step S2/S3. The original is NEVER unlinked by the agent — it is hard-linked into library.trash_dir so the data has two directory entries before the rename overwrites one of them. That link is the entire backstop for invariant I1. `plan_path` produces a collision-free, job-scoped name so a re-dispatch cannot collide with a survivor. `retire` is idempotent for replay: if trash_path already exists and its inode equals the source inode, return `AlreadyLinked` (a crash between link and journal-write replayed); if it exists with a DIFFERENT inode, that is a real conflict and must error rather than silently proceed. `retire` also re-verifies the source fingerprint immediately before linking.

title: CommitPreflight: the ordered gate that must pass before any destructive step
description: A single pure-ish function that composes the checks built in S13-007/008/011 into one ordered verdict, returning the FIRST blocking condition so the operator gets a specific stage rather than a boolean. Fixed evaluation order, which the tests must pin: NotCommitEligible, RenameNotAtomic, WorkAreaCrossDevice, Hardlinked, SourceChanged, FreeSpace. Order matters — checking free space before commit eligibility wastes a statvfs on a node that can never commit, and reporting FreeSpace when the real problem is a cross-device work area sends the operator to buy disks. The only I/O is stat and statvfs; no writes.

title: CommitStep enum and FaultInjector hook
description: Names every point in the ritual at which a crash is possible, and provides the injection hook the crash-matrix test drives. `CommitStep::ALL` is the exhaustive ordered list; the crash-matrix test asserts it covers every variant so a new step cannot be added without a crash test for it. `FaultInjector::check` returns `CommitError::Aborted { step }` when the configured step is reached, simulating a process death right before that step's side effect. `FaultInjector::none()` is the production value and must compile out to a trivially predictable branch (no cfg gating — the ritual always calls check, the default injector always returns Ok).

title: CommitRitual::run — the ordered S0..S6 execution with journal writes between steps
description: Assembles the pieces built above into the ritual. Order, with a FaultInjector::check before each: Preflight (S13-013) -> ValidateOutput (delegated to the injected OutputValidator from S6, never reimplemented here) -> RequestGrant (S13-012) -> fsync temp + write journal phase Granted -> read/apply source attrs (S13-006) -> re-verify source fingerprint then TrashCan::retire (S13-011) -> write journal phase Retired -> AtomicReplacer::install (S13-010) -> write journal phase Installed + fsync final dir -> FinalVerifier probe of the installed path -> return CommitReport. Every journal write precedes the destructive step it authorizes, never follows it. All collaborators are injected as trait objects or generics so the whole thing is testable with no ffmpeg, no gRPC and no real media. Keep this file to orchestration only; if a branch needs more than a few lines of logic it belongs in one of the earlier modules.

title: ReplayResolver: the pure crash-matrix decision function
description: Given a journal record and observed on-disk truth, decide what recovery must do. This is a total, side-effect-free function implementing the architecture's crash matrix exactly, and it is the highest-value unit-test surface in S13 because it encodes the 'never neither' invariant. Rules: phase Granted with final still at source_inode and no trash link -> RollBack. phase Granted with trash link present and final still at source_inode -> RollBack (unlink the redundant link). phase Retired with final still at source_inode -> ResumeAtRename if temp exists and temp_valid, else RollBack (restore from trash). phase Retired with final at a NEW inode and temp gone -> FinishInstall. phase Installed with final at a new inode -> ConfirmInstalled. Any record where final is absent AND trash is absent -> Escalate. No record / no journal file -> DiscardTemp is the caller's default, not this function's concern.

title: ReplayEngine: observe on-disk truth and apply the resolved action
description: The I/O half of recovery, run before the agent registers and before it accepts any work. `observe` stats final/trash/temp and calls the injected validator to set temp_valid. `apply` executes the ReplayAction using fsops with a work-area authorization: RollBack deletes the temp and, if final is not the original inode, restores from trash; ResumeAtRename re-runs AtomicReplacer::install then journals Installed; FinishInstall journals Installed and fsyncs; ConfirmInstalled just journals; Escalate leaves everything untouched and reports. `replay_all` filters the journal to this agent_uid+boot_id namespace only — it must never sweep a shared library root, because two agents can share /mnt/bigdata. Every outcome bumps the recovery counter from S13-019.

title: agent.proto: capability block (decoders, mounts, Capability)
description:
Append the capability messages to `proto/transcodarr/v1/agent.proto` verbatim from the authoritative protocol spec, then regenerate. Purely mechanical transcription - field numbers are load-bearing and must match exactly.

Add, in this order: `enum DecoderKind { DK_SOFTWARE=0; DK_NVDEC=1; DK_QSV=2; DK_VAAPI=3; DK_VIDEOTOOLBOX=4; }`; `enum DecoderStatus { DS_UNTESTED=0; DS_VERIFIED_OK=1; DS_VERIFIED_SOFT_FALLBACK=2; DS_VERIFIED_FAIL=3; }`; `message DecoderTriple { string codec=1; string profile=2; uint32 bit_depth=3; DecoderKind kind=4; }`; `message DecoderCapability { DecoderTriple triple=1; DecoderStatus status=2; string evidence=3; uint64 probed_at_unix=4; }`; `enum RenameProbeStatus { RP_UNTESTED=0; RP_ATOMIC_VERIFIED=1; RP_NOT_ATOMIC=2; }`; `message Mount { string local_path=1; string canonical_prefix=2; string pool_id=3; string fstype=4; uint64 free_bytes=5; uint64 total_bytes=6; bool writable=7; RenameProbeStatus rename_probe=8; map<string,bool> workarea_same_device_by_library=9; }`; `message Capability { string platform=1; string arch=2; string ffmpeg_version=3; string ffprobe_version=4; string nvidia_driver_version=5; uint32 physical_cores=6; double effective_cores=7; repeated string classes=8; repeated string encoders=9; repeated DecoderCapability decoders=10; repeated string muxers=11; repeated Mount mounts=12; uint64 workarea_free_bytes=13; string capability_hash=14; map<string,string> labels=15; }`.

Each enum/message gets a `//` comment carrying the measured rationale: `DS_VERIFIED_SOFT_FALLBACK` = Turing Hi10 h264 (exits 0, decoded on CPU, never satisfies a hardware Decoder requirement); `DS_VERIFIED_FAIL` = Turing AV1 (ffmpeg exit 69, 1 KiB truncated output); `Mount.pool_id` is SERVER-ASSIGNED and echoed back, never `st_dev`; `workarea_same_device_by_library` is resolved per (library root, work dir) against the actual final-path dataset.

Bump the proto file's header `version:` to 1.1.0 and run `cargo run -p xtask -- proto`, committing the regenerated output.

title: Conversions: Mount and Capability
description:
Implement the full capability-document boundary conversion, building on S15-010's decoder conversions.

`crates/transcodarr-proto/src/convert/capability.rs`:
```rust
impl TryFrom<pb::Mount> for transcodarr_core::Mount { type Error = ProtoError; }
impl From<transcodarr_core::Mount> for pb::Mount {}
impl TryFrom<pb::Capability> for transcodarr_core::Capability { type Error = ProtoError; }
impl From<transcodarr_core::Capability> for pb::Capability {}
```
Rules that must be enforced in the `TryFrom` direction and unit-tested:
- An empty `Mount.canonical_prefix` or empty `local_path` is `ProtoError::MissingField`, not a silently accepted empty mount (an empty prefix would make `MountCovers` match everything).
- An empty `Capability.platform` is `MissingField`.
- `effective_cores <= 0.0` or non-finite is `ProtoError::InvalidValue { field: "effective_cores", .. }`.
- `Mount.pool_id` is carried through verbatim as an opaque server-assigned string; the conversion must NOT synthesise one from fstype or device.
- `capability_hash` is carried through verbatim and is NOT recomputed here (recomputation belongs to the core normaliser, so a mismatch stays detectable).
- `classes` entries are parsed into the core `AgentClass` enum; an unknown class string is `ProtoError::UnknownEnum`.
Register the module in `convert/mod.rs`.

title: Conversions: Requirement and Requirements (exhaustive both directions)
description:
Implement the requirement conversions. Correctness here is what makes `satisfies` meaningful: a requirement dropped in translation becomes an unenforced constraint, which is exactly how an agent gets offered work it cannot run.

`crates/transcodarr-proto/src/convert/requirement.rs`:
```rust
impl TryFrom<pb::Requirement> for transcodarr_core::Requirement { type Error = ProtoError; }
impl From<transcodarr_core::Requirement> for pb::Requirement {}
impl TryFrom<pb::Requirements> for transcodarr_core::Requirements { type Error = ProtoError; }
impl From<transcodarr_core::Requirements> for pb::Requirements {}
```
Rules:
- A `pb::Requirement` with `kind == None` (unset oneof) is `ProtoError::UnsetOneof { message: "Requirement", oneof: "kind" }`. It must NEVER be skipped or treated as a vacuous requirement.
- The `From<core>` direction is an exhaustive `match` over `transcodarr_core::Requirement`; because that enum is `#[non_exhaustive]` within its own crate it is still exhaustively matchable here only if core allows it - if a wildcard arm is unavoidable, the wildcard must `unreachable!`-free and instead the function returns `Result` with `ProtoError::InvalidValue`; prefer the exhaustive match and document the compile-error property.
- `MountCovers` carries a canonical path string; empty is `MissingField`.
- `MinFree` with `bytes == 0` is accepted (a zero reserve is legal) but an empty `canonical_path` is `MissingField`.
- `PlatformIn` with an empty `platforms` list is `ProtoError::InvalidValue` (an empty allow-list would match nothing yet reads as "no constraint").
Register the module in `convert/mod.rs`.
