title: Add the xtask crate with a `layering` command that enforces crate dependency direction
description: Create crates/xtask (package name "xtask", not published, binary `xtask`) with dependencies anyhow + toml + serde (workspace). Implement `xtask layering`: walk `crates/*/Cargo.toml`, parse each with the `toml` crate, collect the set of `transcodarr-*` entries under [dependencies], [dev-dependencies] and [build-dependencies], and assert them against a hardcoded allowed-edge table. Allowed edges (dependency -> allowed targets): transcodarr-core -> {} (nothing); transcodarr-proto -> {core}; transcodarr-store -> {core, proto}; transcodarr-server -> {core, proto, store}; transcodarr-agent -> {core, proto} — store is FORBIDDEN; transcodarr-cli -> {core, proto, store, server, agent, testkit}; transcodarr-testkit -> {core}; xtask -> {}. Crates present on disk but absent from the table are an error (so a future crate cannot silently escape the check). Any disallowed edge prints `layering violation: <from> -> <to>` to stderr and the command returns an Err (NOT std::process::exit — that is a clippy disallowed method; return anyhow::Result from main and let the runtime set the exit code). A clean run prints `layering OK: N crates checked`. Add a `.cargo/config.toml` alias `xtask = "run --package xtask --"` so `cargo xtask layering` works. Keep it under ~150 lines; no cargo_metadata dependency, plain TOML parsing only.

Defect 1 (sentinel hack): today `apply_preset` infers 'user did not specify a codec' from `vcodec == "libx264"`, so `--vcodec libx264 --preset original-h265` is silently overridden to libx265. Replace with `Option<&str>` — `None` means unspecified. Defect 2 (silent unknown preset): the `_ => {}` arm makes typos succeed with default codecs; `lookup` must return `Err(PresetError::Unknown)`. Port the three built-in presets and their aliases exactly as they exist today: `original-h265`|`original` => libx265/aac + ["-crf","18","-preset","slow","-b:a","256k"]; `tv-h265-fast`|`tv-fast` => libx265/aac + ["-crf","22","-preset","medium","-b:a","160k"]; `movie-quality`|`movie` => libx265/aac + ["-crf","16","-preset","slow","-b:a","320k"]. Precedence for the resolved codecs, highest first: explicit `Some(x)` argument, then the preset's codec, then the caller-supplied default (the CLI passes libx264/aac for `transcode` and libx265/aac for `batch`, which is why defaults are parameters and not baked in). Extra args: preset extras first, then the user's `extra` appended last so the user can override. `Preset` derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize and is `#[non_exhaustive]`; `PresetError` uses thiserror and is `#[non_exhaustive]`. title: ffprobe fixture corpus A: colour, bit depth and Dolby Vision
description:
Author seven realistic, hand-written ffprobe JSON fixtures covering the colour/bit-depth/DV regression matrix from R70. No Rust code in this task — data only, plus a README describing each fixture's intended verdict.

Each file is the exact stdout of `ffprobe -v error -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <file>`: a top-level object with `streams` (array) and `format` (object). ffprobe emits ALL numerics as JSON strings (e.g. "duration": "1423.360000", "bit_rate": "8412000", "channels" is an integer, "index" is an integer) — reproduce that quirk faithfully, because the parser under test must cope with it.

Required per-stream keys: index (int), codec_name, codec_long_name, codec_type, profile, and for video also width (int), height (int), pix_fmt, bits_per_raw_sample (string), color_range, color_space, color_transfer, color_primaries, r_frame_rate, nb_frames (string); and for audio also sample_fmt, sample_rate (string), channels (int), channel_layout, bit_rate (string). Every stream carries a `disposition` object with at least default/forced/comment integer keys and a `tags` object with `language` and optionally `title`.

Fixtures to create (exact filenames):
1. h264_8bit_aac_stereo.json — h264 High profile, pix_fmt yuv420p, bits_per_raw_sample "8", color_transfer bt709, color_primaries bt709; one aac stereo track. The must-not-be-upconverted case.
2. h264_hi10_aac.json — h264 High 10 profile, pix_fmt yuv420p10le, bits_per_raw_sample "10", bt709 colour; one aac track. The Turing soft-NVDEC-fallback case.
3. hevc_10bit_hdr10_dtshdma_51.json — hevc Main 10, yuv420p10le, color_transfer smpte2084, color_primaries bt2020, color_space bt2020nc; one dts stream with profile "DTS-HD MA", channels 6, channel_layout "5.1(side)".
4. hevc_10bit_hlg_eac3.json — hevc Main 10, color_transfer arib-std-b67, color_primaries bt2020; one eac3 6-channel track.
5. hevc_10bit_dovi_p7_truehd_atmos.json — hevc Main 10 video whose stream object contains a `side_data_list` array with an entry {"side_data_type": "DOVI configuration record", "dv_version_major": 1, "dv_version_minor": 0, "dv_profile": 7, "dv_level": 6, "rpu_present_flag": 1, "el_present_flag": 1, "bl_present_flag": 1, "dv_bl_signal_compatibility_id": 6}; plus a truehd stream with profile "Dolby TrueHD + Dolby Atmos", channels 8.
6. hevc_10bit_dovi_p8_eac3_atmos.json — same shape but dv_profile 8, el_present_flag 0, dv_bl_signal_compatibility_id 1; audio eac3 with profile "Dolby Digital Plus + Dolby Atmos", channels 6.
7. unknown_colour_hevc_10bit.json — hevc Main 10, yuv420p10le, color_primaries bt2020 but color_transfer key ABSENT ENTIRELY and color_space absent; one ac3 track. The Tri::Unknown veto case.

Also create tests/fixtures/ffprobe/README.md listing every fixture in a markdown table with columns: file, video codec, bit depth, expected hdr verdict (yes/no/unknown), expected dovi verdict + profile, audio codecs, why it exists. title: probe kinds: StreamKind, BitDepth and the Tri tri-state
description:
Create the `probe` module and its leaf enum types. This is the first task that touches crates/transcodarr-core/src, so it also creates crates/transcodarr-core/src/probe/mod.rs (declaring submodules and re-exporting) and adds `pub mod probe;` to crates/transcodarr-core/src/lib.rs.

All three types derive Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize with `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`, and are `#[non_exhaustive]` where the architecture calls for growth (StreamKind and BitDepth are NOT non_exhaustive — they are closed sets; Tri is closed too). Every public item needs a `///` doc comment (clippy.toml sets missing-docs-in-crate-items = true).

`Tri` is the explicit tri-state that makes an unknown HDR/DV verdict veto video work rather than silently reading as "no". `vetoes_video()` returns true for both Yes and Unknown — that asymmetry is the whole point of the type and must be covered by a test.

`BitDepth::from_pix_fmt` must be a table lookup over the pixel formats this library actually contains: yuv420p/yuv422p/yuv444p/nv12/nv21/gbrp -> Eight; yuv420p10le/yuv420p10be/yuv422p10le/yuv444p10le/p010le/p010be/gbrp10le -> Ten; yuv420p12le/yuv422p12le/yuv444p12le/p012le -> Twelve; anything else -> Unknown. `from_bits` maps 8/10/12 and everything else to Unknown.

StreamKind::from_codec_type maps ffprobe's codec_type strings video/audio/subtitle/attachment/data; unknown strings return None.

Add inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with the named tests below using inline literals only (no fixture files).

title: serde helpers for ffprobe's string-encoded numerics
description:
ffprobe emits nearly every numeric as a JSON string ("8412000"), sometimes as a bare number, sometimes as the literal "N/A", and rationals as "24000/1001". Write the serde deserialization helpers that absorb all of that so the wire structs in S1-005 can stay declarative.

Create crates/transcodarr-core/src/probe/serde_util.rs with `pub(crate)` deserializer functions usable via `#[serde(deserialize_with = ...)]` and `#[serde(default, deserialize_with = ...)]`. Each helper accepts a JSON string, a JSON number, or null, and treats the strings "N/A", "" and "unknown" (case-insensitive) as absent. Overflow, sign errors and unparseable text yield a serde error carrying the offending text.

Also add `serde` (features ["derive"]) and `serde_json` to crates/transcodarr-core/Cargo.toml `[dependencies]` using `workspace = true` if they are not already present, and bump that file's header version.

`parse_ratio` handles "24000/1001" and "25/1", returning None for a zero denominator (ffprobe emits "0/0" for unset frame rates) — do not divide by zero.

All tests inline, no fixture files.

title: ColorInfo, DoviConfig and the HDR/DV tri-state classifiers
description:
Create crates/transcodarr-core/src/probe/color.rs holding the colour metadata value types and the two classification functions. This is the correctness heart of R42/B5: an unknown verdict must be Tri::Unknown, never Tri::No.

`ColorInfo` holds four Option<String> fields (transfer, primaries, space, range) normalised to lowercase with "unknown"/"reserved"/"N/A"/empty collapsed to None. Provide `ColorInfo::from_raw(&RawStream) -> ColorInfo` and `ColorInfo::is_empty()`.

`classify_hdr(&ColorInfo, depth: BitDepth) -> Tri` rules, applied in order:
- transfer == "smpte2084" or "arib-std-b67" -> Tri::Yes
- transfer is one of bt709, bt470m, bt470bg, smpte170m, smpte240m, linear, iec61966-2-1, bt1361e, log, log100, log316 -> Tri::No
- transfer is None AND primaries == Some("bt2020") -> Tri::Unknown (bt2020 primaries with no transfer is a real, common, ambiguous case)
- transfer is None AND primaries is None AND depth == BitDepth::Ten -> Tri::Unknown (10-bit with no colour metadata at all is not provably SDR)
- transfer is None AND primaries is Some(non-bt2020 SDR primary) -> Tri::No
- transfer is Some(anything else) -> Tri::Unknown

`classify_dovi(side_data: &[RawSideData]) -> (Tri, Option<DoviConfig>)`:
- an entry whose side_data_type contains "DOVI" (case-insensitive) with dv_profile present -> (Tri::Yes, Some(config))
- an entry whose side_data_type contains "DOVI" but dv_profile absent -> (Tri::Unknown, None)
- no DOVI entry at all -> (Tri::No, None)

`DoviConfig { profile: u8, level: u8, rpu_present: bool, el_present: bool, bl_present: bool, bl_signal_compatibility_id: u8 }` derives Debug/Clone/Copy/PartialEq/Eq/Serialize/Deserialize, with `pub const fn is_dual_layer(&self) -> bool` returning true for profile 7 (the B5 veto case) and `pub const fn is_supported_single_layer(&self) -> bool` for profiles 5 and 8.

All tests inline; do not read fixture files here.

title: Normalised Stream domain type
description:
Create crates/transcodarr-core/src/probe/stream.rs: the public, I/O-free, serde-round-trippable per-stream domain type plus its normalisation from RawStream. This is what every later subsystem reads; RawStream must never escape the probe module.

`Stream` derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize. Normalisation rules for `Stream::from_raw(&RawStream) -> Stream`:
- kind: StreamKind::from_codec_type(codec_type).unwrap_or(StreamKind::Data)
- codec / profile: trimmed, lowercased for codec, profile kept in original case (policy matches codecs case-insensitively but profile strings like "High 10" and "Dolby TrueHD + Dolby Atmos" are displayed verbatim)
- bit_depth: prefer bits_per_raw_sample when present and non-zero, else BitDepth::from_pix_fmt(pix_fmt) for video, else BitDepth::from_bits derived from sample_fmt for audio ("s16"->16 is not a BitDepth variant, so audio bit_depth is BitDepth::Unknown unless bits_per_raw_sample says 8/10/12) — document that audio bit depth is informational only
- language: tags lookup that is case-insensitive over the key ("language", "LANGUAGE"), value lowercased, "und" collapsed to None
- title: case-insensitive tags lookup of "title", value verbatim
- duration_s: stream `duration` if present, else parse_hhmmss of a case-insensitive "DURATION" tag
- frame_rate: parse_ratio(avg_frame_rate) falling back to r_frame_rate
- color: ColorInfo::from_raw
- dovi: classify_dovi(&side_data_list).1
- is_default / is_forced / is_comment from disposition

Also provide `Stream::is_object_audio(&self) -> bool`: true when kind == Audio and the profile (lowercased) contains "atmos" or "dts:x" or "dts-x", or codec == "truehd" and channels > Some(8). This is the has_object_audio evidence used by the policy veto.

Tests inline only.

title: MediaProbe assembly and the public parse_ffprobe_json entry point
description:
Finish crates/transcodarr-core/src/probe/mod.rs: define the public `MediaProbe` aggregate and the single public parse entry point named in the architecture contract.

`parse_ffprobe_json(raw: &str) -> Result<MediaProbe, CoreError>` calls parse_raw, returns Err(CoreError::ProbeNoStreams) when the streams array is empty, then normalises every RawStream via Stream::from_raw and assembles the format-level fields.

Format-level derivation rules:
- container: format.format_name split on ',' taking the FIRST token, lowercased and trimmed ("matroska,webm" -> "matroska"); None when absent
- duration_s: format.duration if present and > 0.0; else the maximum Stream::duration_s across all streams; else None. This ordering matters for matroska, which routinely omits format.duration.
- bitrate_bps: format.bit_rate if present; else, when both size_bytes and duration_s are known and duration > 0, compute `(size_bytes * 8) as f64 / duration_s` rounded to u64; else None
- size_bytes: format.size
- tags: format.tags verbatim in a BTreeMap

Helper accessors on MediaProbe (all pure, all documented): `video()` returns the first Video stream, `streams_of(kind)` returns an iterator, `audio_streams()`, `subtitle_streams()`, `count_of(kind) -> u32`.

`MediaProbe` derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize. title: derive_facts: MediaProbe plus size to FileFacts
description:
Implement `derive_facts(probe: &MediaProbe, size_bytes: u64) -> FileFacts` in crates/transcodarr-core/src/facts.rs. Pure function, no I/O, deterministic — the same probe and size must always produce byte-identical output (this is the precondition for R69's determinism property and for content_sig later).

Derivation rules, all from the already-normalised MediaProbe:
- size_bytes: the caller-supplied argument, NOT probe.size_bytes (the probe may be stale or from a different file); container/duration_s/bitrate_bps copied from the probe
- video fields taken from `probe.video()`: codec, profile, bit_depth, pix_fmt, width, height, color
- hdr: `classify_hdr(&video.color, video.bit_depth)` when a video stream exists; Tri::No when there is no video stream at all (an audio-only file cannot have an HDR veto)
- dovi + dovi_profile: from the video stream's `dovi` field — Some(cfg) -> (Tri::Yes, Some(cfg.profile)); None with no video stream -> (Tri::No, None); None with a video stream -> (Tri::No, None). If the video stream's Stream carries no DoviConfig but classify_dovi returned Unknown, that Unknown must survive: thread it through by having Stream expose the Tri verdict too if S1-007 did not — if it did not, add `pub dovi_status: Tri` to Stream in this task and bump stream.rs.
- has_object_audio: any audio stream where `is_object_audio()` is true
- audio_codecs: collect every audio stream's codec, lowercased, sorted ascending, deduplicated (must be stable and deterministic)
- audio_track_count / subtitle_track_count / attachment_count: `probe.count_of(kind)`
- max_audio_channels: max over audio streams' channels, 0 when none
- audio_bytes: sum over audio streams of `bit_rate_bps / 8 * duration` where the stream's own bit_rate_bps is present, using the stream duration if set otherwise the probe duration; None when NO audio stream has a usable bit rate (do not return Some(0) — a missing estimate and a zero-byte estimate mean different things to the audio shrink gate, B6)
- nlink, library_name, canonical_path: left at Default (documented)

Saturating arithmetic throughout; no unwrap on Option, no panic paths, no float NaN propagation (guard duration > 0.0).

title: Pure parser for ffmpeg -progress key=value blocks
description:
Implement the pure parser for the report blocks ffmpeg writes to the file named by `-progress`. Format: repeated `key=value\n` lines, each report terminated by a line `progress=continue` or `progress=end`. No I/O, no async, no allocation of the input.

Quirks that MUST be handled and tested: values may be the literal `N/A` (parse to None, never an error); `speed=1.02x` (strip trailing `x`); `speed=N/A`; `bitrate=1234.5kbits/s` (strip suffix); `total_size` in bytes; `out_time_us` in microseconds; `out_time_ms` which ffmpeg emits in MICROseconds despite the name (treat as microseconds, document the quirk in a /// comment) — if both appear, `out_time_us` wins; `out_time=00:01:23.456789` is ignored (redundant, hh:mm:ss form). Unknown keys are ignored, never an error. A block missing the `progress=` terminator is not a block.

`split_progress_blocks` is the incremental-read primitive: given the accumulated buffer it returns the complete blocks plus the trailing partial remainder the caller must keep for the next read. It must never split a block mid-report even if a read lands between `frame=` and `progress=continue`.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)] #[non_exhaustive] pub struct ProgressFields { pub frame: Option<u64>, pub fps: Option<f64>, pub bitrate_kbps: Option<f64>, pub total_size: Option<u64>, pub out_time_us: Option<u64>, pub dup_frames: Option<u64>, pub drop_frames: Option<u64>, pub speed: Option<f64>, pub marker: ProgressMarker }
pub fn parse_progress_block(block: &str) -> ProgressFields
pub fn split_progress_blocks(buf: &str) -> (Vec<&str>, &str)

title: ProgressAccumulator, ProgressSnapshot and ProgressSummary
description:
Fold parsed ProgressFields into the in-memory snapshot the rest of the agent publishes. Pure (clock is passed in as `now_unix_ms`, never read from the system inside these functions) so it is unit-testable with no sleeping.

Semantics: fields absent from a report retain their previous value (ffmpeg omits keys sporadically); `out_time_us` and `frame` are monotonic — a report with a LOWER value than the current snapshot must be ignored for those two fields (guards against a re-read of an already-consumed prefix). `eta_seconds` = (total_duration_us - out_time_us) / 1e6 / speed, computed only when speed > 0.0 and out_time_us < total_duration_us, else None. `finished` is set when ProgressMarker::End is applied. `summary()` computes avg_fps = frames / wall_seconds and avg_speed = out_time_us / wall_us, both 0.0 when wall time is 0 (never NaN, never a divide-by-zero panic).

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, serde::Serialize)] pub struct ProgressSummary { pub avg_fps: f64, pub avg_speed: f64, pub frames: u64, pub wall_ms: u64 }
pub struct ProgressAccumulator { /* private */ }

impl ProgressAccumulator { pub fn apply(&mut self, fields: &super::progress::ProgressFields, now_unix_ms: u64) -> &ProgressSnapshot }
impl ProgressAccumulator { pub fn snapshot(&self) -> &ProgressSnapshot }
impl ProgressAccumulator { pub fn summary(&self, finished_unix_ms: u64) -> ProgressSummary }

`test_accumulator_eta_uses_speed_and_remaining_duration` asserts a known eta value within 0.01.
`test_accumulator_eta_none_when_speed_zero` asserts eta_seconds is None.
`test_accumulator_summary_zero_wall_time_is_not_nan` asserts avg_fps and avg_speed are finite and 0.0 when started == finished.

title: StallDetector: timeouts keyed on progress advance, not wall clock
description:
The core requirement of this subsystem: a legitimate 12-hour 4K encode must never be killed by a wall-clock timeout, while an ffmpeg wedged on a stale NFS handle must be killed within minutes. Implement a detector whose only liveness evidence is a monotonic increase in `out_time_us` or `frame`.

Pure, deterministic: `now: Instant` is a parameter of both `observe` and `verdict`; the type never calls Instant::now() itself, so tests need no sleeps. `startup_grace` covers the window before ffmpeg emits its first report (probing input, building filter graph). `hard_timeout` is an OPTIONAL absolute ceiling and defaults to None — enabling it by default would reintroduce the wall-clock failure mode this task exists to prevent; document that in a /// comment on the field.

Defaults: stall_timeout 300s, startup_grace 300s, hard_timeout None.
apis: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)] pub struct StallPolicy { pub stall_timeout: std::time::Duration, pub startup_grace: std::time::Duration, pub hard_timeout: Option<std::time::Duration> }
impl Default for StallPolicy
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] #[non_exhaustive] pub enum StallVerdict { Running, Stalled { silent_for: std::time::Duration }, HardTimeout }
pub struct StallDetector { /* private */ }
impl StallDetector { pub fn new(policy: StallPolicy, started_at: std::time::Instant) -> Self }

title: StderrRing bounded 8 KiB stderr tail buffer
description:
A fixed-capacity byte ring that keeps only the LAST N bytes written to it, used to capture ffmpeg stderr for job_attempt.stderr_tail without unbounded memory growth on a chatty encode. Pure, no I/O.

`tail_string` renders with String::from_utf8_lossy and, when the buffer has overflowed at least once, drops everything up to and including the first '\n' so the result never begins with a mangled partial line. Never panics on arbitrary bytes.

title: ExecConfig and prepare_argv: agent-local ffmpeg, no shell, injected -progress
description:
Implement the argv preparation boundary that satisfies R61 (the server supplies arguments only, never an executable) and R19 (argv vector, never a shell string).

`prepare_argv` takes the server's `Assignment.argv` and returns the argument list to pass to the agent-local ffmpeg binary. Rules, each individually tested:
1. Empty input -> Err(ExecError::EmptyArgv).
2. argv[0] is DISCARDED unconditionally — whatever the server sent as the program name is ignored; the program comes from ExecConfig::ffmpeg_path.
3. If the remaining args already contain `-progress`, return Err(ExecError::ProgressFlagInArgv) — the server must not set it and a duplicate would silently redirect our telemetry.
4. The returned vector begins with `-hide_banner`, `-nostats`, `-progress`, <progress_file>, then the server's remaining args in their original order, unmodified. `-hide_banner`/`-nostats` are not duplicated if already present.
5. No element is ever quoted, escaped, joined, or split. Arguments containing spaces, `;`, `$(...)`, `&&`, quotes, and non-ASCII pass through byte-identically.

ExecConfig is the agent-local runtime configuration for this subsystem, deserialisable from the agent TOML.

title: FfmpegProcess: shell-free spawn, piped stderr, SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL
description:
Thin async wrapper over tokio::process::Command. It MUST use Command::new(program).args(args) — the strings `sh -c`, `cmd /c`, and `Stdio::inherit` must not appear in this file. stdin is Stdio::null, stdout is Stdio::null (ffmpeg writes the media to a file, not a pipe), stderr is Stdio::piped so the caller can drain it into a StderrRing. `kill_on_drop(false)` — an orphaned ffmpeg is handled by the inflight journal and adopt-or-kill, not by a Drop impl that would silently destroy work on a task cancellation.

`terminate` sends SIGTERM via `nix::sys::signal::kill` (keeping the crate `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`), waits up to `grace`, then escalates to SIGKILL and waits again. On non-unix, terminate falls back to Child::kill. `wait` maps the ExitStatus to ExitStatusFacts, extracting the terminating signal on unix via std::os::unix::process::ExitStatusExt.

`nice` is applied on unix with `nix::unistd::nice` inside a `pre_exec`-free path — implement it by setting the priority in the parent for the child via `Command::process_group(0)` is NOT sufficient, so instead accept the simpler contract: if `nice` is Some and the platform is unix, prepend nothing and instead call `nix::sys::resource`/setpriority on the spawned pid immediately after spawn (best-effort; a failure is logged at warn and is NOT an error).

title: InflightRecord and InflightJournal with fsync-before-exec durability
description:
The durability primitive that makes adopt-or-kill possible: a per-attempt JSON record fsynced to disk BEFORE ffmpeg is spawned, so a crash in the microsecond after fork still leaves evidence that a process may exist and a temp file may need cleaning.

Two-phase because the pid is not known until after spawn: `reserve()` writes the record with `pid: None` and fsyncs (this is the pre-exec write); `record_pid()` rewrites it with the pid and start-ticks and fsyncs again. Both writes are write-temp + fsync(temp) + rename + fsync(dir) so a torn record is impossible.

File layout: `<dir>/<job_id>-<attempt>.json`. `dir` is the agent's own state dir, namespaced by agent_uid and boot_id by the CALLER — this type never invents paths outside `dir`. `list()` skips and warn-logs unparseable files rather than failing the whole replay (a single corrupt record must not brick agent startup). `remove()` is idempotent: removing a nonexistent entry is Ok(()).

title: Process liveness with pid-reuse protection
description:
Answer 'is the ffmpeg recorded in this journal entry still the process running under that pid?' A bare kill(pid, 0) is not enough — pids are reused, and killing a reused pid on a 48-core box that has spawned thousands of processes would be a genuine outage. Guard with the process start time.

On Linux read field 22 (starttime, in clock ticks since boot) from /proc/<pid>/stat. That field must be parsed by locating the LAST ')' in the line first, because the comm field (field 2) may itself contain spaces and parentheses — a naive whitespace split is wrong and must be covered by a test using a synthetic stat line. Also expose the resolved executable from /proc/<pid>/exe so callers can sanity-check it is really ffmpeg.

On non-Linux targets every function returns None / Liveness::Unknown; callers treat Unknown conservatively (see S12-010).

title: AdoptDecision table: pure adopt-or-kill policy
description:
The pure decision function for restart reconciliation, separated from the I/O that carries it out so the whole policy is a table test with no filesystem and no processes.

Rules, in this exact order:
1. `record.agent_uid != ctx.agent_uid` -> Discard { reason: "foreign_agent_uid" }. An agent must NEVER touch another agent's records or files even when two agents share a library root (this is the A10/A11 guard).
2. `record.pid.is_none()` -> CleanOnly. reserve() succeeded but the spawn never completed (or we crashed between the two writes); no process can be running under our record, but a temp file may exist.
3. liveness Dead -> CleanOnly.
4. liveness Unknown -> KillAndClean when policy.kill_on_unknown_liveness (default TRUE), else CleanOnly. Conservative default: on a platform where we cannot prove the process is gone, we must not leave an ffmpeg writing to a temp file we are about to delete.
5. liveness Alive && record.boot_id == ctx.boot_id -> Adopt { pid }. Same process instance: this is a stream reconnect, the job never stopped.
6. liveness Alive && different boot_id && policy.adopt_across_restart (default TRUE) -> Adopt { pid }. The agent process restarted but ffmpeg survived; because progress goes to a FILE and not a pipe, the tailer can resume reading it. This is why the design uses -progress <file>.
7. liveness Alive && different boot_id && !adopt_across_restart -> KillAndClean { pid }.

Adoption caveat to document in a /// comment: an adopted process is not our child, so waitpid is unavailable; the caller must poll liveness plus the progress file rather than awaiting an exit status.

title: reconcile_inflight: apply adopt decisions on startup
description:
Execute the decisions from S12-010 against the real filesystem and real processes, and return the records that should be re-adopted so the runtime can restart their tailers.

For each journal record: compute liveness (using record.pid_start_ticks), call decide(), then
- Adopt -> leave everything on disk, push the record into the returned Vec.
- KillAndClean -> SIGTERM the pid, wait up to `grace`, SIGKILL, then clean.
- CleanOnly -> clean.
- Discard -> touch nothing at all, not even the journal entry.
Clean means: delete `temp_output` if present, delete `progress_file` if present, then `journal.remove(job_id, attempt)`.

SAFETY INVARIANT, enforced in code and by test: `source_path` is NEVER deleted, and no path outside `temp_output`/`progress_file` is ever unlinked. A `debug_assert` plus an explicit runtime check that the path being removed equals one of those two fields; a mismatch returns Err rather than deleting.

Errors on an individual record are logged at warn and collected into the report — one bad record must not abort startup reconciliation.

title: ProgressTailer: async incremental read of the -progress file
description:
A tokio task that polls the progress FILE (never a pipe — a file is what makes adoption across an agent restart possible) at `interval`, reads only the bytes after its last offset, splits complete blocks with split_progress_blocks, folds them through the ProgressAccumulator, and publishes the latest snapshot to a tokio::sync::watch channel.

Required behaviours: the file may not exist yet when the tailer starts (ffmpeg creates it) — that is Running, not an error, and the tailer retries each tick. A read error is logged at warn and retried, never fatal. The trailing partial block is retained across ticks. Publishing is last-value-wins via watch, so a slow consumer never applies backpressure and no progress event is ever queued or written to a database (R56/T6). The task ends when `progress=end` is applied OR the handle is stopped; `stop()` performs one final read so the last report is never lost.

`ProgressTailerHandle::snapshot()` is a cheap borrow of the watch value for the InflightTable and Heartbeat paths.

title: InflightTable: agent-side registry of running jobs and their snapshots
description:
The agent's in-memory view of what it is currently running. Backed by a plain std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<(u64, u32), JobHandle>> — the single-owner/no-Mutex discipline applies to the server's Dispatcher module, not here, and avoiding a new dashmap dependency keeps the agent small for the WSL2 node.

`cancel` triggers the CancellationToken; `kill_immediately` is stored on the handle so the Executor's cancel branch knows whether to use a zero grace. All lock scopes must be short and must never be held across an .await (clippy::await_holding_lock is denied by -D warnings).

title: Executor::run — orchestrate journal, spawn, tail, stall, terminate
description:
Wire the pieces together. This is the only integrating task in S12 and it writes no new algorithms — every decision it makes is delegated to a type built in an earlier task, which is why it stays small.

Exact ordering (a test asserts the journal write precedes the spawn):
1. `prepare_argv` (S12-006).
2. Delete any stale progress file at paths.progress_file.
3. `journal.reserve(record)` with pid None — fsynced BEFORE exec.
4. `FfmpegProcess::spawn`.
5. `journal.record_pid(pid, process_start_ticks(pid))`.
6. Drain stderr into a StderrRing on a spawned task.
7. `spawn_tailer` with a fresh ProgressAccumulator; insert a JobHandle into the InflightTable.
8. `tokio::select!` over: process exit; a stall-check interval tick that feeds the latest snapshot to the StallDetector; the CancellationToken.
9. On StallVerdict::Stalled or HardTimeout -> terminate(cfg.terminate_grace), set outcome.stall_terminated = true. On cancel -> terminate with grace 0 if kill_immediately else cfg.terminate_grace, set cancelled = true.
10. Stop the tailer (final read), collect the stderr tail, remove from InflightTable, `journal.remove(...)`, return ExecOutcome.

Executor::run does NOT validate the output, does NOT rename anything, and does NOT classify the failure — validation and the commit ritual are separate subsystems, and classify_failure lives in transcodarr-core. The ExecOutcome carries exactly the evidence those callers need.

On any early-return error path after step 3 the journal entry MUST be left in place so startup reconciliation can clean it; only a normal completion removes it.

title: fake_ffmpeg test double and executor integration tests
description:
A deterministic stand-in for ffmpeg so the executor's behaviours can be tested in CI with no media, no GPU, and no real encoder. Python per the repo rule that scripts over ~20-30 lines are Python (see scripts/generate_test_media.py for the header/style precedent).

scripts/fake_ffmpeg.py accepts the real ffmpeg flags it needs to look authentic (`-hide_banner`, `-nostats`, `-progress <file>`) plus test-control flags read from environment variables so they never collide with the argv-passthrough test: FAKE_FFMPEG_BLOCKS (number of progress reports), FAKE_FFMPEG_INTERVAL_MS, FAKE_FFMPEG_EXIT (exit code), FAKE_FFMPEG_STALL_AFTER (emit N blocks then sleep forever without further progress), FAKE_FFMPEG_STDERR_BYTES, FAKE_FFMPEG_ECHO_ARGV_TO (write the received argv as JSON to this path), FAKE_FFMPEG_OUTPUT_BYTES (write that many bytes to the last argv element). It writes well-formed progress blocks ending in `progress=continue`, with a final `progress=end`.

The integration test file drives Executor with program = python3 + the script, skipping with `eprintln!("SKIP: python3 not available")` when python3 is absent, matching the repo's ffmpeg_available() guard pattern.

title: EpochTracker: fencing epoch bumps only on new process instance
description: Owns the fencing epoch on the agent side. The epoch is authoritative from `RegisterResponse.fencing_epoch`; a stream reconnect within the SAME process (same boot_id) must resume the existing epoch and must never renegotiate it upward locally (fix C9). If `Welcome.fencing_epoch` differs from what the agent sent in `Hello`, the server has fenced this instance: the verdict is `Fenced`, and the caller must abandon all in-flight jobs without committing. Also exposes the staleness predicate used to refuse assignments and to reject commits.

title: Outbound lanes: lossless control channel, lossy progress channel, monotonic seq
description: The priority outbound multiplexer. `JobResult`, `CommitIntentOpen`, `JobAccepted`/`JobRejected`, `JobStarted`, `DrainStatus`, `Hello` and `Heartbeat` are LOSSLESS: the sender awaits a full channel. `Progress` and `LogLines` are LOSSY: `try_send`, dropped on congestion, counted. `OutboundMux::next` always drains the lossless queue before the lossy one and stamps a monotonic `seq` starting at 1. This is the structure that makes a slow browser or a congested link unable to stall a job result.

title: Assignment vetting: re-validate requirements, epoch, duplicate job, path roots
description: Pure defence-in-depth gate run on every received `Assignment`, using the SAME `transcodarr_core::satisfies` the server used, so any rejection is by definition a stale server capability model (alarmed as a server bug, never absorbed as a routine retry). Check order is fixed: (1) stale fencing epoch -> reject non-transient; (2) job_id already running -> reject non-transient; (3) `satisfies(cap, requirements)` -> reject non-transient with the serialized `UnmetRequirement`; (4) `guard_within_roots` on all six paths in `JobPaths` -> reject `path_outside_roots`; (5) accept. Transient rejections (mount momentarily gone, encoder sessions exhausted) are produced by the caller, not here.

title: Hello/Welcome handshake over the Connect stream
description: After `Register` succeeds and the stream opens, send `Hello{identity, capability_hash, fencing_epoch, running_job_ids}` and await `Welcome`. The first inbound message MUST be a Welcome; anything else is a protocol error and the stream is dropped. title: Register call: build request, negotiate versions, apply intent resolutions

title: Drainer: stop accepting, emit DrainStatus, grace expiry
description: Drain semantics for `DrainRequest`, `Shutdown` and SIGTERM. Once draining, the agent accepts no new assignments, emits a `DrainStatus` after every job completion, and exits at zero running jobs. On grace expiry it cancels everything and deletes every temp — never leaving a partial file. Reducing capacity is drain, never cancel: nothing in this type may cancel a job before grace expiry. Pure state machine plus a `now: Instant` parameter so it is testable without sleeping.

title: CleanupTemp and Revoke handling
description: Execute the two destructive control messages safely. `CleanupTemp` deletes named temps/job work dirs, but every path is re-checked with `guard_within_roots` AND must live inside this agent's own `agent_uid`+`boot_id` work namespace, so two agents sharing a library root can never GC each other's live work. title: Server: pool-scoped byte budget
description: Implement the fourth limit: a byte budget scoped to a server-assigned PoolId, never to a mount path or st_dev (U0, U1 and the WSL2 node see the same physical ZFS pool under three different device numbers, so per-mount budgeting would triple-count the same free bytes). title: Server: large-file bucket with per-class reservations and shed
description: Implement the cluster-global large-file bucket. A single flat global cap is Tdarr failure mode 5 in miniature (3 large audio jobs would lock out every large video job indefinitely), so slots are partitioned: each class may hold up to its reserved count unconditionally, and the remaining unreserved slots are first-come. Admission rule, implement exactly: let `total = sum(occupied)`, `unreserved_capacity = slots.saturating_sub(sum(reserve))`, `reserved_remaining(c) = reserve[c].saturating_sub(occupied[c])`, `unreserved_used = sum over c of occupied[c].saturating_sub(reserve[c])`; then `admits(c) == total < effective_slots && (reserved_remaining(c) > 0 || unreserved_used < unreserved_capacity)`. Also implement adaptive shed: `set_shed(level)` lowers effective slots to `max(1, slots - level)` — shed refuses NEW acquisitions only and must never reduce `occupied`. `set_limits` likewise may leave `occupied > effective_slots`; that is a legal, observable, transient drain state, not an error.

title: Server: per-agent and global per-class slot counters
description: Implement the first two of the four limits as plain counters in a `SlotTable`: per-(agent, class) slots (bounds a machine-local resource such as NVENC sessions or CPU threads) and cluster-global per-class slots (bounds encoder demand across machines). No Arc, no Mutex, no atomics, no Semaphore — the table is owned by value by the Dispatcher, so acquisition is a synchronous counter bump. An agent/class pair with no configured limit has 0 slots and never admits. `set_limits` replaces the configured limits and deliberately does NOT touch occupancy: reducing a limit at a quiet-hours boundary must drain, never cancel, so `occupied > configured` is legal and is reported by `over_limit`. Provide `iter_agent_slots` for the metrics exporter (S18-009).

title: Server: CapacityLedger peek/acquire/release composition
description: Compose SlotTable, LargeBucket and the per-pool PoolBudget map into the single `CapacityLedger` the Dispatcher owns by value. `peek` checks all four limits in a fixed order and returns the FIRST failing one as a BlockStage so the operator never has to guess which cap is holding a job; order is exactly: agent slot -> `BlockStage::NoFreeSlot`, global class -> `GlobalClassLimit`, large bucket (only when `size_bucket == Large`) -> `LargeFileLimit`, pool byte budget -> `FreeSpace`. `acquire` is infallible once `peek` returned Ok in the same synchronous round: it bumps all four counters and returns `AcquiredPermits` minted via `permits::mint`, and it must `debug_assert!` that `peek` currently returns Ok (an all-or-nothing guarantee with no partial-acquire path — there is no code path that takes three permits and waits for a fourth). `release` consumes the permit, decrements exactly the counters that were incremented, and is called on LEAVING the admitted state set (Assigned|Running|Verifying|Committing), not on reaching a terminal state. `set_limits` forwards to SlotTable and LargeBucket without touching occupancy. Also expose `update_pool_free_bytes` (called from agent heartbeats) and `set_large_shed`. This file must contain no `.await`, no rusqlite, no std::fs.

pub struct CapacityLedger { /* private: slots: SlotTable, large: LargeBucket, pools: BTreeMap<PoolId, PoolBudget>, limits: EffectiveLimits */ }

title: Store + server: rebuild ledger from admitted jobs on boot
description: Close the boot-time hole: if the ledger starts empty while the database still holds jobs in the admitted set, the server double-commits capacity. Add one indexed store query returning the admitted rows, and the ledger constructor that replays them. Store side: `JobRepo::admitted_jobs` runs a single SELECT joining `library` for the pool id — `SELECT j.id, j.agent_id, j.class, j.size_bucket, j.input_bytes, j.state, l.pool_id FROM job j JOIN library l ON l.id = j.library_id WHERE j.state IN ('Assigned','Running','Verifying','Committing') AND j.agent_id IS NOT NULL` (served by `idx_job_state`) and maps each row to `transcodarr_core::capacity::AdmittedJobRow`, computing `projected_bytes` with the same `projected_bytes(class, input_bytes, expansion_factor)` rule (pass the factor in as an argument so store does not depend on server; treat NULL `input_bytes` as 0). Server side: `CapacityLedger::rebuild_from_store(rows, limits)` constructs a ledger and applies one acquire per row WITHOUT consulting `peek` — the DB is authoritative and may legitimately exceed current limits after a config change while the server was down. Rows for an agent or pool not present in `limits` are still counted (they hold real resources); log a warn once per unknown key. Return the ledger plus the count so the caller can log it.

title: authorize_register gating function (pure)
description: Implement the single authorization decision point as a pure function with no I/O and no async. It enforces, IN THIS EXACT ORDER, four rules and returns the first failure: (1) under `PeerIdentity::Mtls`, `common_name` must equal `req.identity.agent_id`, else `AuthError::CnMismatch`; under `Token` no CN check applies; (2) `req.identity.proto_version` must be within `[gate.min_supported_proto, gate.server_proto_version]`, else `ProtoTooOld`/`ProtoTooNew`; (3) `req.identity.agent_version` parsed as semver must be `>= gate.min_agent_version`, else `AgentVersionTooOld` (an unparseable version is `MalformedIdentity`); (4) agent_uid pinning: if `known` is Some with a different `agent_uid` AND `live_uid` is Some (a session is currently live for this agent_id), return `DuplicateAgentIdentity`; a different agent_uid with `live_uid == None` is an accepted reinstall. Empty `agent_id`, `agent_uid` or `boot_id` is `MalformedIdentity`. On success return the domain `AgentIdentity`. Add `semver = "1"` to `[workspace.dependencies]`. Do NOT touch the database here — `known` and `live_uid` are supplied by the caller.

title: LeaseTracker in server monotonic time
description: Track agent liveness using ONLY server-side `Instant` values taken at message arrival — an agent's wall clock and the `Heartbeat.monotonic_ms` field must never influence expiry, because the WSL2 node's clock jumps across host sleep/resume. Implement a per-agent state machine over three durations: `lease` (default 30s), `grace` (reconnect_grace, default 300s) and heartbeat interval (informational). `observe_heartbeat` records arrival and, if the entry was `Expired`, emits `Restored`. `on_stream_closed` sets `Expired { since: now }` immediately (a closed stream is treated as instant lease expiry, faster than TTL). `tick(now)` scans and emits `Unhealthy` for entries whose `last_seen + lease < now` and `GraceElapsed` exactly once for entries expired longer than `grace`. Every transition is emitted at most once per state entry. All methods take `now: Instant` so tests are deterministic without sleeping.

title: Agent-loss orphan reconciliation and Revoke
description: Handle what happens to an agent's in-flight work when its lease expires and the reconnect grace elapses. On `LeaseTransition::Unhealthy`: mark the agent Unhealthy, halt dispatch to it, but touch NO jobs (the agent may reconnect and re-claim). On `LeaseTransition::GraceElapsed`: for each job this agent holds, release its `AcquiredPermits` (emit `DispatchEvent::SlotReleased`), append `job_event { reason_code: "lease_expired" }`, and transition `Assigned|Running|Verifying` -> `Retrying` with `FailureCode::AgentLost` (transient, consumes an attempt). `Committing` jobs are NEVER auto-requeued while a live `commit_intent` exists — they are left alone for intent resolution. Then enqueue a `Revoke { job_ids, new_fencing_epoch, reason }` to be delivered on the agent's next connect, bumping the epoch so any late `ReportCommit` from the old instance is rejected as `TransitionError::FencingStale`. Increment `transcodarr_orphans_reconciled_total{kind}` with `kind` in {lease, temp, intent}. All job transitions go through `JobRepo::transition` compare-and-swap; a lost CAS is a logged no-op, never a corruption.

title: Core: DaysMask + ScheduleWindow activity predicate (midnight wrap)
description:
Create the pure, I/O-free schedule window primitives in transcodarr-core. No tokio, no rusqlite, no tonic. This task is ONLY the types plus the activity predicate; limit merging is S21-002 and TOML shapes are S21-003.

Implement:
- `pub struct DaysMask(u8);` bit 0 = Monday .. bit 6 = Sunday. Methods: `pub const fn from_bits(bits: u8) -> Self`, `pub const fn bits(self) -> u8`, `pub const fn contains(self, weekday: Weekday) -> bool`, `pub const ALL: DaysMask`.
- `#[non_exhaustive] pub enum Weekday { Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun }` with `pub const fn index(self) -> u8` (Mon=0) and `pub const fn from_index(i: u8) -> Option<Weekday>`.
- `pub struct MinuteOfDay(u16);` with `pub fn new(m: u16) -> Result<Self, CoreError>` rejecting >= 1440, `pub const fn get(self) -> u16`.
- `pub struct ScheduleWindow { pub id: i64, pub name: String, pub enabled: bool, pub days: DaysMask, pub start: MinuteOfDay, pub end: MinuteOfDay, pub priority: i64, pub overrides: LimitOverridesDoc }` where `LimitOverridesDoc` is a newtype over `serde_json::Value` in THIS task (S21-002 replaces it with the typed form; keep the field name stable).
- `pub fn window_active(w: &ScheduleWindow, weekday: Weekday, minute: MinuteOfDay) -> bool` — false when `!w.enabled` or `!w.days.contains(weekday)`; otherwise if `start < end` active iff `start <= minute < end`; if `start >= end` (wraps midnight) active iff `minute >= start || minute < end`. `start == end` means the window is never active (document this explicitly in the rustdoc).
- `pub fn select_active<'a>(windows: &'a [ScheduleWindow], weekday: Weekday, minute: MinuteOfDay) -> Option<&'a ScheduleWindow>` — lowest `priority` value wins; ties broken by lowest `id` so selection is deterministic.

All public items need `///` docs (clippy `missing-docs-in-crate-items = true`). Derive Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq where possible, and serde Serialize/Deserialize on ScheduleWindow, DaysMask, MinuteOfDay, Weekday.

title: Core: BaseLimits, LimitOverrides, EffectiveLimits and the merge function
description:
Add the typed limit model and the pure merge function to transcodarr-core. This is the single source of truth for what a slot count is; the server never computes limits by hand.

Implement in crates/transcodarr-core/src/schedule/limits.rs:
- `pub struct BaseLimits { pub per_agent: BTreeMap<(AgentId, JobClass), u32>, pub global_class: BTreeMap<JobClass, u32>, pub global_large: u32, pub large_reserve: BTreeMap<JobClass, u32> }`. Use the existing `AgentId` and `JobClass` types from transcodarr-core; if `AgentId` does not yet exist, add `pub struct AgentId(pub String)` in this task with Ord/Clone/serde.
- `pub struct LimitOverrides { pub per_agent: BTreeMap<(AgentId, JobClass), u32>, pub global_class: BTreeMap<JobClass, u32>, pub global_large: Option<u32> }` — every field is a sparse patch; absent means "inherit".
- `pub struct EffectiveLimits { ... same shape as BaseLimits ... }` with `pub fn agent_slots(&self, agent: &AgentId, class: JobClass) -> u32`, `pub fn global_class(&self, class: JobClass) -> u32`, `pub fn global_large(&self) -> u32`.
- `pub fn merge_limits(base: &BaseLimits, layers: &[LimitOverrides]) -> EffectiveLimits` — layers applied in order, LAST wins per key. Absent keys inherit from base. Values are replacements, never deltas.
- `pub fn diff_limits(a: &EffectiveLimits, b: &EffectiveLimits) -> Vec<LimitChange>` where `pub struct LimitChange { pub scope: String, pub class: Option<JobClass>, pub from: u32, pub to: u32 }` — used by the engine to decide whether to emit an event and by the UI to show what a window did.

title: Core: TOML deserialization of [[schedule_window]] blocks
description:
Make the operator-facing TOML in the architecture document parse into the S21-001/S21-002 types. Purely serde plus small parsers; no file I/O.

Target shape that must round-trip:
```toml
[[schedule_window]]
name     = "quiet-hours"
days     = ["mon","tue","wed","thu","fri","sat","sun"]
start    = "23:00"
end      = "07:00"
priority = 10
[schedule_window.overrides."agent:u1"]
video_cpu = 1
audio     = 8
[schedule_window.overrides.global]
large = 1
```

Implement in crates/transcodarr-core/src/schedule/toml_shape.rs:
- `pub struct ScheduleWindowToml { pub name: String, #[serde(default = "default_true")] pub enabled: bool, pub days: Vec<String>, pub start: String, pub end: String, #[serde(default = "default_priority")] pub priority: i64, #[serde(default)] pub overrides: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, u32>> }`.
- `pub fn parse_hhmm(s: &str) -> Result<MinuteOfDay, CoreError>` accepting exactly `HH:MM` 00:00..=23:59; reject `24:00`, `7:00` (unpadded is REJECTED — be strict), `23:60`, and anything else.
- `pub fn parse_days(days: &[String]) -> Result<DaysMask, CoreError>` accepting case-insensitive `mon|tue|wed|thu|fri|sat|sun`; unknown name is an error naming the offending token.
- `pub fn parse_scope(key: &str) -> Result<Scope, CoreError>` where `#[non_exhaustive] pub enum Scope { Global, Agent(AgentId) }`; accepts `"global"` or `"agent:<id>"`; rejects empty agent id and any other prefix. Also `impl Display for Scope` producing the same strings (round-trip).
- `pub fn overrides_from_toml(map: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, u32>>) -> Result<LimitOverrides, CoreError>` — inner keys are JobClass names in snake_case (`audio`, `video_gpu`, `video_cpu`, `probe`, `verify`) plus the special key `large` which is only legal under scope `global` and maps to `global_large`. Unknown class names are an error, never silently ignored.
- `pub fn window_from_toml(id: i64, t: &ScheduleWindowToml) -> Result<ScheduleWindow, CoreError>` tying it together, replacing the S21-001 placeholder `LimitOverridesDoc` field with the typed `LimitOverrides` from S21-002.

title: Core: ScheduleOverride with mandatory expiry and relative `until` parsing
description:
Temporary overrides must always expire — a permanent pause is forbidden by design. This task is the pure domain type plus the `until` parser used by the API.

Implement in crates/transcodarr-core/src/schedule/overrides.rs:
- `pub struct ScheduleOverride { pub id: i64, pub scope: Scope, pub class: Option<JobClass>, pub slots: u32, pub expires_unix: i64, pub actor: Option<String>, pub reason: Option<String>, pub created_unix: i64 }`.
- `pub fn parse_until(s: &str, now_unix: i64) -> Result<i64, CoreError>` — accepts a relative duration `+<n><unit>` with unit in `s|m|h|d` (e.g. `+2h`, `+30m`, `+7d`) resolved against `now_unix`, or a bare RFC3339 / unix-seconds integer absolute timestamp. Rejects: missing `+` on a relative form, zero or negative durations, a resolved instant `<= now_unix`, and anything beyond `max_until_secs` (parameter, default 30 days) so nobody can set a 100-year "temporary" override.
- `pub fn overrides_to_layer(list: &[ScheduleOverride], now_unix: i64) -> LimitOverrides` — filters out rows with `expires_unix <= now_unix`, then folds the survivors into one `LimitOverrides` layer, ordered by ascending `id` so a later override wins over an earlier one for the same (scope, class). `class == None` combined with `Scope::Global` maps to `global_large`; `class == Some(c)` with `Scope::Global` maps to `global_class[c]`; `Scope::Agent(a)` with `class == Some(c)` maps to `per_agent[(a,c)]`; `Scope::Agent(_)` with `class == None` is dropped and counted (return it in a second tuple element `Vec<i64>` of rejected ids rather than panicking — signature: `-> (LimitOverrides, Vec<i64>)`).
- `pub fn validate_slots(slots: u32, force: bool) -> Result<(), CoreError>` — a value of `0` is rejected unless `force` is true, with the error message explaining that silently stopping a class is indistinguishable from a bug.
apis: pub fn parse_until(s: &str, now_unix: i64, max_until_secs: i64) -> Result<i64, CoreError>
pub fn overrides_to_layer(list: &[ScheduleOverride], now_unix: i64) -> (LimitOverrides, Vec<i64>)
pub fn validate_slots(slots: u32, force: bool) -> Result<(), CoreError>
pub struct ScheduleOverride

title: Server: config validation with zero-limit and inline-secret guards
description:
Pure-ish validation of a candidate config TOML, used by both `POST /api/v1/config/validate` and the apply path. This task does NOT do the policy dry-run diff (that belongs to the policy subsystem) — it validates structure, limits and secrets only, and returns a struct the diff can be attached to later.

Implement in crates/transcodarr-server/src/config/validate.rs:
- `pub struct ConfigValidation { pub valid: bool, pub rules_version: RulesVersion, pub errors: Vec<ConfigError>, pub warnings: Vec<String>, pub windows: Vec<ScheduleWindow>, pub base_limits: BaseLimits }`
- `pub struct ConfigError { pub path: String, pub message: String }` — `path` is a dotted TOML path such as `schedule_window[0].start` so the UI can point at the offending line.
- `pub fn validate_config(toml_text: &str, opts: &ValidateOpts) -> ConfigValidation` where `pub struct ValidateOpts { pub force: bool, pub known_agent_ids: Vec<AgentId> }`.

Rules enforced, each producing a distinct ConfigError:
1. TOML parses; unknown top-level keys are a WARNING, unknown keys inside `[limits]` / `[[schedule_window]]` are ERRORS (serde `deny_unknown_fields` on those structs).
2. Any inline credential — a `token`, `api_token`, `auth_token`, or `*_key` string value under `[security]` — is a hard ERROR pointing the operator at `token_file`.
3. Every `[[schedule_window]]` parses via `window_from_toml`; each error is surfaced with its index.
4. `validate_slots(n, opts.force)` is applied to EVERY slot value in base limits and in every window override: a 0 without `force` is an error naming the exact scope and class.
5. Every `agent:<id>` override scope whose id is not in `known_agent_ids` is a WARNING, not an error (an agent may simply be offline right now).
6. `global.large.reserve` values must sum to <= `global.large.slots`, else ERROR.

title: Server: ConfigManager with ArcSwap, apply and change notification
description:
Hot reload without restarting the server or disconnecting agents. `ConfigManager` owns the live config and is the ONLY writer of `config_revision` rows.

Implement in crates/transcodarr-server/src/config/manager.rs:
- `pub struct ConfigManager { current: ArcSwap<LiveConfig>, writer: WriterHandle, read_pool: ReadPool, tx: watch::Sender<ConfigGeneration> }`
- `pub struct LiveConfig { pub revision_id: i64, pub rules_version: RulesVersion, pub toml: String, pub base_limits: BaseLimits, pub windows: Vec<ScheduleWindow>, pub runtime: RuntimeConfigTemplate }` where `RuntimeConfigTemplate` holds the agent-facing knobs (`progress_interval_ms`, `heartbeat_interval_ms`, `lease_seconds`, `min_free_reserve_bytes`, `default_nice`, `log_level`).
- `pub async fn load(read_pool: ReadPool, writer: WriterHandle, bootstrap_toml: &str) -> Result<Arc<Self>, ConfigError>` — reads `ConfigRepo::latest_revision()`; if none exists, validates and inserts `bootstrap_toml` with `ConfigSource::Bootstrap`.
- `pub fn current(&self) -> Arc<LiveConfig>` — lock-free `ArcSwap::load_full`.
- `pub async fn apply(&self, req: ApplyRequest) -> Result<AppliedConfig, ConfigError>` where `ApplyRequest { toml: String, actor: Option<String>, note: Option<String>, source: ConfigSource, force: bool, expected_rules_version: Option<RulesVersion> }`. Sequence, in this exact order: validate (S21-007) → if `expected_rules_version` is `Some` and does not match the candidate's computed `rules_version`, return `ConfigError::StalePreview` → one `WriteLane::Commit` transaction that inserts the `config_revision` row AND calls `ScheduleRepo::replace_windows` → swap the `ArcSwap` → `watch::Sender::send` a bumped `ConfigGeneration`. A failed validation or a failed transaction leaves the live config untouched.
- `pub fn subscribe(&self) -> watch::Receiver<ConfigGeneration>`

`apply` MUST NOT cancel, kill, or requeue any job, and MUST NOT close any agent stream. State that in the rustdoc.

title: Server: ScheduleEngine recompute loop with injectable clock
description:
The engine is the only thing that turns "what time is it" into `EffectiveLimits`. It must be testable without sleeping, so time is injected.

Implement in crates/transcodarr-server/src/schedule/engine.rs:
- `pub trait Clock: Send + Sync { fn now_unix(&self) -> i64; fn local_weekday_and_minute(&self) -> (Weekday, MinuteOfDay); }` plus `pub struct SystemClock;` and `pub struct FixedClock { pub unix: AtomicI64, pub weekday: Weekday, pub minute: u16 }` (test double, `#[cfg(test)]` not required — it is useful for `admin` too).

- `pub fn recompute(&self) -> Result<RecomputeOutcome, ScheduleError>` — SYNCHRONOUS and side-effect-light: reads the live `BaseLimits` and windows from `ConfigManager::current()`, reads unexpired overrides via `ScheduleRepo::list_unexpired_overrides(now)` (caller supplies them through a small `OverrideSource` closure/trait so the test does not need a DB), selects the active window with `select_active`, builds the layer list `[window_overrides, override_layer]`, calls `merge_limits`, and swaps `effective`. Returns `RecomputeOutcome { changed: bool, changes: Vec<LimitChange>, active_window: Option<String> }`.
- `pub async fn run(self: Arc<Self>, shutdown: CancellationToken)` — loop that recomputes on: a 30s tick, every schedule-window boundary minute (compute the sleep to the next boundary rather than polling every second), and every `ConfigManager::subscribe()` notification. - `pub fn effective(&self) -> Arc<EffectiveLimits>`

The engine NEVER cancels a job and has no code path to `CancelJob`.

description:

title: Integration test: quiet-hours end-to-end drain-not-cancel scenario
description:
One scenario test that proves the whole S21 subsystem composes correctly. This is the acceptance artifact for the subsystem; it uses fakes, not real agents or ffmpeg.

Implement in crates/transcodarr-server/tests/schedule_integration.rs:
Arrange — temp SQLite DB with migrations, a `ConfigManager` bootstrapped from a TOML with `agent.u1.video_cpu = 4` plus the quiet-hours window setting `agent:u1 video_cpu = 1`, a `FixedClock` set to 22:55 Monday, a `ScheduleEngine`, a `Dispatcher` with a `CapacityLedger`, and one `FakeAgent` `u1` with a bounded channel.

Act/Assert, in order:
1. At 22:55 `effective().agent_slots(u1, video_cpu) == 4`; acquire 4 permits.
2. Advance the FixedClock to 23:05 and call `recompute()`; assert `changed == true` and `effective().agent_slots(u1, video_cpu) == 1`.
3. Assert all 4 permits are STILL held, no `CancelJob` was sent to the FakeAgent, and `over_limit()` reports `{u1, video_cpu, occupied: 4, configured: 1}`.
4. Assert the FakeAgent received exactly one `ServerMessage::RuntimeConfig` with `slots_by_class["video_cpu"] == 1`.
5. Release 3 permits; assert `peek(u1, video_cpu, Small)` still returns `Err(BlockStage::NoFreeSlot)` (occupied 1, configured 1).
6. Release the last permit; assert `peek` returns `Ok(())`.
7. Advance the clock to 07:05 Tuesday, recompute, assert slots are back to 4 and a second RuntimeConfig push occurred.
8. Post an override `{scope:"agent:u1", class:"video_cpu", slots:0, until:"+2h"}` without force through the API and assert HTTP 400; repeat with `?force=true` and assert 200/201 and `effective().agent_slots(u1, video_cpu) == 0` after recompute.

title: Pure crash-matrix resolver in transcodarr-core (recovery module)
description: Create the pure, I/O-free decision function that decides how a live commit intent resolves, given its recorded phase and the observed on-disk state. This is the correctness heart of S20 and must be unit-testable with zero DB, zero filesystem and zero network. No tokio, no rusqlite, no tonic may be referenced. Encode the crash matrix from the architecture verbatim: Granted -> roll back; Retired + temp still validates + final inode still equals recorded source inode -> roll forward; Retired + temp invalid + trash present -> restore from trash; Retired + final inode differs from recorded source inode -> confirm installed; Installed + final probes to recorded output -> confirm; final missing AND trash missing -> escalate. title: LeaseSweeper: periodic lease expiry with grace and Committing exclusion
description: Implement the 5s lease pass. Query JobRepo::list_lease_expired(now, batch_limit). Rules, all mandatory: (1) if in_recovery_grace(now) is true, do nothing and count skipped_grace — a reconnecting agent must be able to re-claim its work rather than have it duplicated; (2) a job in Committing with has_live_intent == true is NEVER auto-requeued, count skipped_committing — the replace window may be half done and only the intent ledger may resolve it; (3) Assigned/Running/Verifying transition to Retrying with FailureClass::Transient / FailureCode::AgentLost (consumes an attempt) via JobRepo::transition inside one Writer transaction that also appends job_event with reason_code "lease_expired"; (4) for each requeued job emit DispatchEvent::SlotReleased so the CapacityLedger releases the permits, and call record_orphan_reconciled(OrphanKind::Lease). Leases are compared entirely in server time — do not read any agent-supplied wall clock.

impl Reconciler { pub(crate) async fn sweep_leases(&mut self, now_unix: i64) -> Result<SweepStats, ReconcileError> }

title: Intent recovery from agent replay: plan_resolutions
description: Turn the live commit_intent rows plus an agent's replayed IntentJournal (RegisterRequest.live_intents) into a list of planned resolutions using transcodarr_core::recovery::resolve_intent. Matching is strict: an intent may only be paired with a replay entry on exactly (job_id, attempt) AND the intent's agent_uid/boot_id equalling the registering agent's — never on path or spec resemblance. A replay entry bearing a fencing_epoch that is not the intent's current epoch yields IntentResolution::Escalate. Live intents with no matching replay entry are left untouched here (S20-009 owns them). This task is the planning half only: it is a pure-ish function over rows, so it must be unit-testable with in-memory vectors and no DB.

title: Apply planned resolutions transactionally with metrics
description: Execute the PlannedResolution list produced by S20-008. Each resolution is applied in ONE Writer transaction on WriteLane::Commit (synchronous=FULL): CommitIntentRepo::resolve(...) plus the job CAS transition (job_to) plus the job_event row with reason_code equal to the resolution label, plus — for ConfirmInstalled / RollForward — the write-through of the output probe into file/file_stream if the agent supplied one. Increment record_intent_recovered(action) and record_orphan_reconciled(OrphanKind::Intent), and refresh set_live_intents(). Application must be idempotent: re-applying an already-resolved intent is a no-op that still returns Ok. A lost CAS (TransitionError::Lost) is logged at warn and skipped, never retried in a loop.

title: Unclaimed intents: Verify-job enqueue and NeedsOperator escalation
description: Handle live intents whose owning agent never came back. On each tick, for every live intent whose owning agent has been disconnected longer than reconnect_grace: enqueue a JobClass::Verify job (requirements = [MountCovers(final_path), AgentClass matching a commit_eligible agent]) whose result decides roll-forward vs roll-back; if no connected agent's mount table covers the final path, or if a previous Verify job for that intent already failed, resolve the intent 'escalated', transition the owning job to NeedsOperator with reason_code 'commit_ambiguous', and refresh set_needs_operator(). An intent must never be auto-resolved by guessing. Never sweep by walking a shared library root — selection is driven purely by the ledger rows scoped to (agent_uid, boot_id).

title: Orphan temp cleanup planner (server side)
description: Compute the CleanupTemp message the server sends an agent on reconnect and after lease loss. A job id may only be listed for cleanup if: the server does not consider it open for THAT agent, it has no live commit_intent, and the temp path lies within that agent's own (agent_uid, boot_id) work namespace. This is the fix for the shared-root sweep hazard: one agent must never be told to delete another agent's in-flight temp. Pure planning function plus a thin Reconciler wrapper that loads the inputs; the actual unlink happens agent-side in S20-012.

title: TrashReaper pass (server selects, agent unlinks)
description: Implement the trash reaper pass. Normal path: TrashRepo::list_purgeable(now, batch_limit). Pressure path: when a pool's free_bytes minus reserve_bytes is below threshold, additionally take list_pressure_candidates(pool_id, now - trash_min_grace, ...) — the min_grace floor is absolute and must never be bypassed. The server MUST NOT unlink the files itself (the destructive-call grep forbids it): it sends the selected trash paths as a CleanupTemp message to a commit_eligible agent whose mounts cover the pool, and only calls TrashRepo::mark_purged after that agent acknowledges. Refresh set_trash_totals() and record_orphan_reconciled(OrphanKind::Trash) after each reap.

title: ConsistencyChecker: fsck invariant I1 and friends

Each violation increments transcodarr_invariant_violations_total. Scope is selectable so the periodic pass can check only live intents (cheap, every fsck_interval) while an operator can request All. title: Operator resolution path for NeedsOperator intents

title: BlockStage enum with exhaustive as_label()
description: Create the BlockStage enum that names every reason the dispatcher can refuse to place a job. This is the label vocabulary for transcodarr_dispatch_blocked_total{stage} and the dispatch_block.blocking_stage column, so the snake_case spellings are a wire/schema contract and must not drift. Implement as_label() as a `const fn` with an exhaustive match (no `_ =>` arm) so adding a variant without a label is a compile error. Also implement Display via as_label, serde Serialize/Deserialize with #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")], and mark the enum #[non_exhaustive] per rust.instructions.md. Add a const ALL: &[BlockStage] slice listing every variant, used by tests and later by the /diagnose exhaustiveness check. No other dispatcher code depends on anything but this file, so it ships first. File header comment (file/version 1.0.0/new guid) required; document every public item with /// because clippy.toml sets missing-docs-in-crate-items.

title: DispatchEvent, DispatchStats, DispatcherSnapshot value types
description: Define the three plain data types the dispatcher exchanges with the rest of the server. DispatchEvent is the wakeup vocabulary delivered over an mpsc channel (the dispatcher never polls the DB). DispatchStats is accumulated on the stack during one round; the dispatcher must not touch the metrics registry inside its critical section. DispatcherSnapshot is what a 1s exporter task reads via ArcSwap. All three are pure structs/enums with derives only - no logic, no I/O, no async. DispatchEvent is #[non_exhaustive]. Keep DispatcherSnapshot cheap to clone (counts and small maps only, no job payloads).

title: BucketKey: blake3 over categorical requirements only
description: Implement BucketKey, the partition key that keeps the matcher O(buckets) instead of O(queue). It is blake3 over ONLY the categorical requirements - AgentClass, Encoder, Decoder(triple), Muxer, PlatformIn, LabelEquals - and must deliberately EXCLUDE MinFreeBytes, MinEffectiveCores and MountCovers, because those carry per-file byte counts and per-file paths and would explode cardinality toward one bucket per job (flaw A5). Canonicalise before hashing: collect the categorical requirements into a sorted, deduplicated Vec of stable string encodings, join with a 0x1F separator, then blake3. The encoding must be stable across process runs (no HashMap iteration order, no Debug formatting of floats). The function is total and infallible. Requirements/Requirement come from transcodarr-core (S3); match exhaustively over Requirement so a new variant forces an explicit include/exclude decision.

impl BucketKey { pub fn from_requirements(req: &Requirements) -> BucketKey; pub fn to_hex(self) -> String; }

title: EligibilityBitset and RequirementBucket recompute
description: Implement the cached per-bucket agent mask. EligibilityBitset wraps a bitvec indexed by AgentIdx (a dense index into AgentTable, added in S19-007 - for this task accept a plain usize index and a slice of (AgentIdx, &Capability, &[(Requirement,bool)] overrides)). RequirementBucket holds the BucketKey, the representative categorical Requirements, and the cached bitset. recompute() calls transcodarr_core::satisfies (S3) per agent, ANDs in any agent_capability_override rows whose `allowed = false` for a requirement present in this bucket, and sets/clears bits. Critically the bitset is a FILTER, never a GRANT: document on the type that a stale bitset may only lose throughput and can never produce a bad match, because find_candidate re-runs the full verify before constructing an Assignment. Volatile facts (free bytes, mount freshness, nlink) must NOT enter the bitset (flaw A6) - assert this in a doc comment and keep recompute's signature free of any heartbeat/mount argument so it is structurally impossible.

title: ReadyJob, ReadyQueue heap and SkipCursor
description: Implement one queue partition. ReadyJob is the dispatcher's in-memory view of an Eligible job: id, file_id, class, size_bucket, priority, order_key (epoch millis), bucket_key, requirements, input_bytes, projected_bytes, canonical_path, pool_id, excluded_agents. ReadyQueue holds BinaryHeap<Reverse<(u32 priority, i64 order_key, JobId)>> so pop order is (priority ASC, order_key ASC, id ASC) - FIFO by enqueue time. There must be NO smallest-first-by-size ordering anywhere: add a doc comment stating that Tdarr failure mode 6 is unrepresentable here and a test asserting a 100 GiB job enqueued first is popped before a 1 GiB job enqueued second. SkipCursor tracks a bounded backfill position: `advance()` moves past a head that failed admission, `reset()` on any successful assignment or new insert, and `skipped()` reports how many heads have been passed this round so find_candidate can stop at K. Because BinaryHeap cannot peek past the head, implement peek_n(k) by draining up to k entries into a scratch Vec held on the queue and restoring them - document the k<=64 bound that keeps this O(k log n).

impl SkipCursor { pub fn advance(&mut self); pub fn reset(&mut self); pub fn skipped(&self) -> u32; }

impl ReadyQueue { pub fn push(&mut self, priority: u32, order_key: i64, id: JobId); pub fn remove(&mut self, id: JobId) -> bool; pub fn len(&self) -> usize; pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool; pub fn peek_n(&mut self, k: usize) -> Vec<JobId>; pub fn oldest_order_key(&mut self) -> Option<i64>; pub fn cursor_mut(&mut self) -> &mut SkipCursor; }

title: ReadyIndex: partitioned queues, job map, bucket index
description: Implement ReadyIndex, the dispatcher's whole view of eligible work. It owns queues: HashMap<(JobClass, SizeBucket), ReadyQueue>, jobs: HashMap<JobId, ReadyJob>, and by_bucket: HashMap<BucketKey, Vec<JobId>>. Partitioning by (class, size_bucket) is the structural fix for head-of-line blocking (flaw A9): an inadmissible Large head must be physically incapable of sitting in front of Small work. hydrate() ingests a batch of ReadyJob values produced elsewhere by QueueFeeder (the dispatcher never issues SQL) and returns the set of BucketKeys that were newly created, so the caller can emit DispatchEvent::BucketCreated and no bucket is invisible for a round (flaw C1). take(job_id) removes a job from all three structures atomically. depth_by_partition() and oldest_age_ms(now) feed the snapshot gauges.

AgentTable stores entries in a Vec indexed by AgentIdx with a HashMap<AgentId, AgentIdx> side index, so AgentIdx stays dense and stable for the bitsets in S19-004. Provide rotate_from(cursor) yielding AgentIdx values starting at cursor and wrapping, which is how the round-robin cursor stops one agent from always winning the scan. accepts_work() on AdminState and a classes_with_free_slot(idx) helper. There must be no Default, no from_job, no force flag, no pub field, and no #[derive(Deserialize)] that could bypass the constructor. Add module docs stating the four claims and pointing at the tests. Also confirm here (by test, not comment) that a DecoderStatus::VerifiedSoftFallback capability does not satisfy a Requirement::Decoder whose kind != Software - the Turing Hi10 lesson - even though the rule itself is implemented in core; if core's behaviour ever changes, this test fails in the dispatcher where it matters.

title: AdmissionCheck: volatile per-job gates evaluated at selection time
description: Implement the per-job checks that must NOT be cached in the bucket bitset because they change between rounds (flaw A6). admit() is a pure function of (ReadyJob, AgentEntry latest-heartbeat mounts, PoolBudgetView, now) returning Result<(), BlockStage>. Checks, in this order, each mapping to exactly one BlockStage: agent not in job.excluded_agents (NoAgentWithCapability), agent.commit_eligible when the job class mutates media (NotCommitEligible), a mount covering the job's canonical path exists and is writable (PathTranslation), that mount's workarea_same_device flag for this library is true (WorkAreaCrossDevice), mount observation is fresher than mount_staleness (default 30s) (PathTranslation), and pool free bytes minus reserve minus outstanding admits projected_bytes (FreeSpace). Ordering matters for the operator: the first failing check is what dispatch_block records. No filesystem calls, no DB, no clock reads beyond the passed-in `now`.

title: Dispatch-time path translation and argv materialization
description: Turn a matched (ReadyJob, AgentEntry) pair into the concrete payload the agent execs. Uses the agent's PathTranslator (core, S3) to map the canonical source, work dir, temp output, final output, progress file and trash dir into agent-local paths - /mnt/bigdata on U0 and U1 but /mnt/bd inside WSL2 - then calls transcodarr_core::build_ffmpeg_argv to produce the argv Vec<String>. Any translation failure returns Err(BlockStage::PathTranslation) so it is a dispatch-time ineligibility and never a runtime job failure (R21, flaw D4). Temp paths must be namespaced by job_id + attempt + agent_uid so a re-dispatch cannot collide with a survivor of a previous attempt (flaw B14). argv[0] is emitted as the literal "ffmpeg" placeholder and documented as discarded by the agent, which substitutes its own configured binary path (R61).

title: AssignmentWriter trait, CAS commit payload, and fake for tests

AND state='Eligible'` plus a job_event row plus a job_attempt row containing the exact translated argv written BEFORE the agent runs it. title: requeue_job: back-of-queue order_key and agent exclusion

On a capability-class rejection the rejecting agent is appended to excluded_agents (deduplicated) and the exclusion is cleared once every eligible agent has been tried; on a transient rejection excluded_agents is NOT touched (flaw A13). RequeueRequest is the struct the AssignmentWriter port carries.

title: DispatchBlockRecorder: bounded per-job block rows
description: Implement the recorder that makes every non-dispatch written rather than inferred. During a round the dispatcher calls record(job_id, stage, per-agent UnmetRequirement details) into an in-round buffer keyed by JobId (a HashMap, so at most one row per queued job - bounded by queue size, self-cleaning). At end of round flush() converts the buffer into Vec<DispatchBlockRow> for AssignmentWriter::record_blocks and increments transcodarr_dispatch_blocked_total{stage} from the accumulated DispatchStats. The recorder must cap the per-agent detail list at max_detail_agents (default 8) so detail_json stays small, and must record only the FIRST (most informative, earliest-stage) reason per job per round rather than overwriting with later ones. No metrics calls happen inside record(); they happen in flush(), after the critical section.

title: find_candidate: bitset filter, bounded skip, backfill, starvation escape
description: Implement candidate selection for one (agent, class) pair. Walk the partitions for that class in size_bucket order the ledger peek permits, take up to K = 64 heads from ReadyIndex::peek_partition, and for each: skip fast if the bucket's EligibilityBitset clears this agent's bit, then run the FULL verify() (never trust the bitset as a grant), then run admit(). An inadmissible head advances the SkipCursor and the scan continues rather than aborting (flaw C3). If the partition is fully skipped and agent.idle_since exceeds starvation_grace (default 1s) while the partition is non-empty, perform an unbounded scan for that agent on the next call. An always-admit-one escape guarantees forward progress: if every head is inadmissible for the same reason across the whole partition, return Err with that stage so it is recorded once. Returns the chosen JobId plus the Verified witness so the caller can construct an Assignment without re-verifying.

pub struct Candidate { pub job_id: JobId, pub verified: Verified, pub size_bucket: SizeBucket }

title: dispatch_round: agent-first loop with zero .await
description: Implement the synchronous critical section. For each agent from rotate_from(round_robin_cursor): skip unless admin_state.accepts_work() and status == Online; for each class with a free slot: call ledger.peek() for ALL FOUR permits before selecting (flaw D6) and record the returned BlockStage on the head job if it fails; check schedule.allows(); call find_candidate; on success acquire the permits, take the job from ReadyIndex, materialize argv, construct Assignment via Assignment::new, submit CommitAssignRequest through AssignmentWriter, and only then try_send the ServerMessage. A full channel is never awaited: mark the agent Unhealthy, release the permits, requeue via requeue_job(transient=true) and increment transcodarr_agent_rejections_total{reason="channel_full"} (flaw A7). A CommitAssignError::LostCas releases permits and advances the SkipCursor so a job that repeatedly loses the CAS cannot pin the head. The function signature must be `fn dispatch_round(&mut self) -> DispatchStats` - not async - and its body must contain no `.await`, no DB call, no filesystem call, and no synchronous logging to a slow sink; timing is captured with Instant and published later.
