title: Dispatcher struct, event loop, and 5s unconditional safety pass
description: Assemble the owning task. Dispatcher holds ledger, agents, ready, buckets, events receiver, writer, round_robin_cursor and dirty flag BY VALUE - no Arc, no Mutex, no atomics in the hot structures. run() is the only async function: select over the DispatchEvent channel and a 5s interval tick, set dirty on any event, call dispatch_round when dirty or when the unconditional safety tick fires (flaw B11 - a lost health edge must not wedge the queue), then publish a DispatcherSnapshot via ArcSwap and record transcodarr_dispatch_last_pass_unix and the round-duration histogram AFTER the round returns. Handle each DispatchEvent: AgentConnected/CapabilityUpdate recompute the affected bitsets, BucketCreated recomputes the new bucket immediately, AgentDisconnected removes the agent and releases its permits, ConfigApplied/ScheduleTick just set dirty. Graceful shutdown on a CancellationToken.

title: Idempotent deployment installer script (Python)
description: Write `scripts/install_deploy.py`, an idempotent installer for the systemd artifacts. Python is mandatory here (repo rule: Python for anything past ~20-30 lines with filesystem/error handling). Subcommands via argparse: `install --role server|agent [--prefix /usr/local] [--dry-run]` and `verify --role ...`. Behaviour: create the `transcodarr` system user/group if absent; create /etc/transcodarr (0755) and the state dir (0700); copy the unit(s) from deploy/systemd/ to /etc/systemd/system only when content differs (hash compare, print `unchanged` otherwise); create token files with mode 0600 if missing and never overwrite an existing one; run `systemctl daemon-reload` only when a unit actually changed. title: ApiError enum and JSON error envelope
description:

- `pub struct ErrorEnvelope { error: ErrorBody }` and `pub struct ErrorBody { code: String, message: String, detail: serde_json::Value }`, both `Serialize`.
- `impl ApiError { pub fn code(&self) -> &str; pub fn status(&self) -> axum::http::StatusCode; }` — `code()` is a stable snake_case string (`not_found`, `bad_request`, `job_not_retryable` etc. taken from the variant's `code` field where present, else the variant name snake_cased).

- `pub type ApiResult<T> = Result<T, ApiError>;`

Internal/Store errors must log at `error!` with the source chain but MUST NOT leak the source string into `message` (use a fixed "internal server error" message and put nothing in `detail`). All other variants may echo their detail.

title: Job mutation routes: cancel, retry, bulk-retry
description:
Add mutation handlers to crates/transcodarr-server/src/api/jobs.rs (or jobs_mutate.rs if over 300 lines). All mutating verbs are idempotent-safe: acting on an already-satisfied target returns 200 with the resulting object, never 409.
- `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` body `{ reason: String, kill_immediately?: bool }` -> transitions an open job to `Cancelled` with `reason_code = "operator_cancel"` via `JobRepo::transition` (CAS), emits a `CancelJob` toward the owning agent through `dispatch_tx`, returns the updated `JobSummary`. Cancelling an already-`Cancelled` job returns 200 unchanged. Cancelling a job in any other terminal state returns 409 `job_terminal`.
- `POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/retry` body `{ reset_excluded_agents?: bool }` -> MUST NOT mutate the terminal row. Inserts a NEW `job` row with `parent_job_id = {id}`, state `Pending`, `attempt = 0`, freshly re-planned `plan_json`/`expected_content_sig` from the file's current stored facts, and `excluded_agents_json` either copied or reset per the flag. Returns the new `JobSummary` (201). Retrying a non-terminal job returns 409 `job_not_retryable` with `detail.state`.
- `POST /api/v1/jobs/bulk-retry` body `{ failure_code?: String, class?: String, limit: u16 }` (limit <= 500) -> applies the same single-retry logic to matching `DeadLettered` jobs, returns `{ created: [job_id] }`. Never touches non-DeadLettered rows.

Retry must call the same planner function `derive_retry_job()` and must NOT share a code path with `requeue_job()`.

title: ui/router.js hash router with view lifecycle
description:
Create `ui/router.js` (3-line header). Pure ES module importing only `./dom.js`. Hash-based routing so no server rewrite rules are needed beyond the SPA fallback. Export:

```js
/** loader: () => Promise<{ mount(el, ctx): void|Promise<void>, unmount?(): void }> */
export function registerRoute(pattern, loader);   // pattern like "/", "/agents", "/jobs/:id"
export function start(rootEl, { notFound } = {});  // binds hashchange, performs first navigation
export function navigate(hash);                    // sets location.hash
export function currentRoute();                    // { pattern, path, params, query } | null
export function parseHash(hash);                   // pure: "#/jobs/88213?tab=logs" -> { path:"/jobs/88213", query:{tab:"logs"} }
export function matchRoute(pattern, path);         // pure: ("/jobs/:id","/jobs/88213") -> {id:"88213"}; null on no match
```

title: ui/sse.js live event stream client
description:
Create `ui/sse.js` (3-line header), importing only `./api.js` (for `getToken`). Wraps `GET /api/v1/events?topics=...`. Because `EventSource` cannot set an Authorization header, append the token as a query parameter `?access_token=<tok>` when a token exists, and document that requirement in the module comment so the S23 API task keeps accepting it. Export:

```js
export function open(topics = ["progress","jobs","agents"], { jobId } = {}); // idempotent: reopening with the same args is a no-op
export function close();
export function subscribe(eventName, handler);  // eventName: "progress"|"job"|"agent"|"resync"|"log"|"status"; returns an unsubscribe function
export function status();                        // "connecting" | "open" | "closed"
```

Behaviour: parse each event's `data` as JSON and fan out to subscribers; a handler that throws must be caught and logged, never breaking the fan-out. On stream error, set status `connecting`, close the EventSource, and reconnect with backoff `min(1000 * 2^n, 30000)` and ±50% jitter. On reconnect, emit a synthetic `resync` event with `{ reason: "reconnected" }` so views refetch. Emit a `status` event on every status change (used by `#conn-status`). Never buffer more than the latest payload per `job_id` for `progress` — expose `latestProgress(jobId)` returning the last snapshot or null, so a view that mounts mid-stream can paint immediately.

title: ValidationGate enum, GateOutcome and ValidationReport
description: Create the gate identity and result-accumulator types. ValidationGate is #[non_exhaustive] with exactly eleven variants in this canonical order: ExitCode, Probe, MinBytes, DecodeNull, Duration, StreamCounts, EmptyStream, TrackIdentity, BitDepth, HdrPreserved, Size. Size MUST be last -- this ordering is the structural answer to a truncated output being smaller than its source. Provide `pub const ORDER: [ValidationGate; 11]` listing them in that order, `pub const fn as_label(self) -> &'static str` returning stable snake_case strings (exit_code, probe, min_bytes, decode_null, duration, stream_counts, empty_stream, track_identity, bit_depth, hdr_preserved, size) used verbatim as the Prometheus label value for transcodarr_validation_failures_total{gate}, and `pub const fn is_corruption_gate(self) -> bool` returning true for every variant except Size. Both const fns use exhaustive match so adding a variant is a compile error. title: Decode-null gate and its argv builder
description: The decode-null gate is the only check that reads every byte of the output and is what catches mid-file corruption that duration and stream counts miss. title: validate_output orchestrator with short-circuit ordering
description: Wire the eleven gates into the single entry point that both the server and the agent call, so agent-side re-validation runs literally the same bytes as server-side validation. Define ValidationInputs<'a> { pub exit: &'a ExitStatusFacts, pub output_probe: Option<&'a MediaProbe>, pub output_bytes: u64, pub output_audio_bytes: Option<u64>, pub decode_null: Option<&'a DecodeNullResult> } and pub fn validate_output(spec: &ValidationSpec, inputs: &ValidationInputs<'_>) -> ValidationReport. Iterate ValidationGate::ORDER and dispatch each variant to its gate function via an exhaustive match so a new variant cannot be added without wiring it. Push every outcome into the report and STOP at the first Failed -- gates after a failure are not evaluated and are absent from the report entirely (not recorded as Skipped), because an unparseable probe makes every later gate meaningless. Gates from Duration onward require a MediaProbe; since Probe runs at position 2 and short-circuits, the later gates can unwrap the probe safely, but express that with a let-else that pushes a Failed rather than a panic. Because Size is last and short-circuiting stops at the first failure, ValidationReport::kept_original_no_gain() is true exactly when the output is valid but did not shrink.

title: FailureClass and FailureCode with retryability predicates
description: Define the taxonomy that drives every scheduling decision after a job ends. FailureClass is #[non_exhaustive] with Transient, Terminal, Capability, Validation, Cancelled. The single most important assignment: EncoderSessionExhausted MUST map to Transient, NOT Capability. It looks like HwEncodeUnavailable but denylisting hevc_nvenc on the only GPU agent in the cluster turns every future GPU job into an instant dead-letter -- a self-inflicted outage. title: classify_failure ordered pattern table
description: Implement pub fn classify_failure(exit_code: i32, signal: Option<i32>, stderr_tail: &str) -> (FailureClass, FailureCode) as an explicitly ordered, first-match-wins table over a lowercased copy of stderr_tail. Order matters and is the correctness content of this task; encode it as a const slice of (needle, FailureClass, FailureCode) walked in order, with the signal and exit-code special cases handled before the table. Required ordering and mappings, top to bottom: signal Some(15) -> (Cancelled, Cancelled); signal Some(9) -> (Transient, AgentLost); any other Some(signal) -> (Transient, IoError); exit_code == 0 with no signal -> (Terminal, Unknown) documented as a caller programming error. Then the needle table, in this exact order: "openencodesessionex" and "no free encoding sessions" -> (Transient, EncoderSessionExhausted) -- these MUST precede the encoder-unavailable needles; "cannot load nvcuda", "no capable devices found", "cannot init cuda", "nvenc" combined with "not supported" -> (Capability, HwEncodeUnavailable); "hwaccel initialisation returned error", "failed setup for format cuda", "no decoder surfaces left" -> (Capability, HwDecodeUnsupported); "no space left on device" -> (Transient, DiskFull); "stale file handle" -> (Transient, NfsStale); "input/output error", "transport endpoint is not connected" -> (Transient, IoError); "invalid data found when processing input", "moov atom not found", "end of file" -> (Terminal, InputUnreadable); "incompatible pixel format", "pixel format" with "not supported" -> (Terminal, InvalidPixFmt). After the table, exit_code == 69 -> (Capability, HwDecodeUnsupported), which is the measured Turing AV1 hard failure. Default fallthrough -> (Transient, Unknown): an unrecognised error retries a bounded number of times rather than dead-lettering immediately.

title: RetryConfig and deterministic backoff_delay
description: Implement the pure backoff computation with injected jitter so it is unit-testable without a random source. Define RetryConfig { pub base: std::time::Duration, pub max: std::time::Duration, pub jitter_frac: f64, pub max_attempts: u32 } with Default = base 30s, max 30m, jitter_frac 0.5, max_attempts 3, deriving Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Serialize/Deserialize. Implement pub fn backoff_delay(attempt: u32, cfg: &RetryConfig, jitter_unit: f64) -> std::time::Duration where jitter_unit is a caller-supplied value clamped into [0.0, 1.0]. Computation: raw = cfg.base * 2^(attempt.saturating_sub(1)), saturating at cfg.max BEFORE jitter is applied; scale = 1.0 - jitter_frac + 2.0 * jitter_frac * jitter_unit; result = raw * scale, then clamp the final value to at most cfg.max * (1.0 + jitter_frac) and at least Duration::ZERO. attempt == 0 returns Duration::ZERO. Use checked exponentiation so a large attempt number saturates rather than overflowing. Also add pub const fn should_dead_letter(attempt: u32, cfg: &RetryConfig) -> bool returning attempt >= cfg.max_attempts. This function must be called only for FailureClass values whose uses_backoff() is true; document that Capability failures pass not_before_unix = 0 instead.

description: Bridge the validation subsystem to the failure taxonomy so the caller never re-derives the mapping. Define #[non_exhaustive] pub enum ValidationOutcome { Accepted, KeptOriginalNoGain { detail: String }, Rejected { class: FailureClass, code: FailureCode, gate: ValidationGate, detail: String } } and pub fn outcome_for(report: &ValidationReport) -> ValidationOutcome. Logic: if report.accepted() return Accepted; if report.kept_original_no_gain() return KeptOriginalNoGain carrying the Size gate's detail -- this is a SUCCESS outcome, the temp is deleted, the original is untouched and a per-decision-class skip marker is written, and it must never be reported as a failure; otherwise take report.first_failure() and return Rejected with gate set to that gate, code = FailureCode::ValidationGateFailed(gate), class = FailureClass::Validation, and detail copied from the outcome. A report with no gates at all returns Rejected with gate Probe and a detail of 'empty validation report'. Add pub const fn is_success(&self) -> bool on ValidationOutcome returning true for Accepted and KeptOriginalNoGain.
apis: pub enum ValidationOutcome
pub fn outcome_for(report: &ValidationReport) -> ValidationOutcome
impl ValidationOutcome { pub const fn is_success(&self) -> bool }

title: R70 validation regression fixture suite
description: Add an integration test file exercising validate_output and classify_failure against synthetic MediaProbe values built in code -- no media files, no network, no DB, no ffmpeg. Add a small fixture builder module with helpers such as probe_with(video: VideoSpecArgs, audio: &[AudioSpecArgs], subtitle: usize) so each test reads as three lines of Arrange. Every test uses explicit // Arrange, // Act, // Assert comments, snake_case names, and a message string on every assert, matching the existing tests/integration_tests.rs style. Required cases, each mapping to a failure already observed in production: a multi-audio-track plus multi-subtitle file whose output dropped all but the default audio track fails StreamCounts; a 10-bit HEVC source whose output is 8-bit fails BitDepth; an 8-bit source whose output was upconverted to 10-bit fails BitDepth; an HDR10 file whose output lost smpte2084 fails HdrPreserved; a deliberately truncated output that is 40 minutes short of a 3-hour source fails Duration and the report contains no Size entry, proving the size guard alone would have accepted it; an AV1 hard-failure attempt with exit 69 and a 1024-byte output fails ExitCode and classify_failure returns (Capability, HwDecodeUnsupported); a Hi10 soft-fallback attempt that exited 0 with 'hwaccel initialisation returned error' in stderr produces a passing validation but classify_failure on that stderr still reports HwDecodeUnsupported when the exit was nonzero; an audio-only EAC3 pass that grew the file passes with Accepted under MayGrow/AudioStreamsOnly.
apis: fn probe_with(...) -> MediaProbe (test-only fixture builder)
acceptance: All eight named cases exist as separate #[test] fns with these exact names: test_multitrack_audio_dropped_fails_stream_counts, test_ten_bit_source_downconverted_fails_bit_depth, test_eight_bit_source_upconverted_fails_bit_depth, test_hdr10_transfer_lost_fails_hdr_preserved, test_truncated_output_fails_duration_before_size, test_av1_exit_69_fails_exit_code_and_classifies_capability, test_hi10_soft_fallback_stderr_classifies_hw_decode_unsupported, test_audio_pass_that_grew_file_is_accepted

Every test uses // Arrange // Act // Assert comments and every assert carries a message string

title: Public API surface, re-exports and module docs
